I prove an exact weighted codimension formula for order-`s` vanishing on a lifted line-polynomial graph. It gives a characteristic-free transfer rule: `n` distinct accepted crossings force a target-line identity when `sn>D`. However, the interpolation cost is quadratic in `s`, so the normalized degree `D/s` remains on the scale `sqrt(dr)`. With the Kominers--Thaler--Zheng reference guarantee `r<=6400p/epsilon` and root budget `n=Omega(epsilon p)`, this reproduces the cubic condition `epsilon^3=Omega(d/p)`.\n\nThere is a second, structural failure. For `s>=2`, removing the coefficient gcd does not turn a jet interpolant into a simple-root explainer: every first derivative, including the vertical derivative, still vanishes on every nontrivial seed graph. Thus uniform multiplicity is not a drop-in improvement to the KTZ pipeline.\n\nFinally, the campaign's explicit endpoint `d=0` is false. For every integer `k>=2` and every prime `p>=max{50,8k!}`, there is a constant line table with local agreement at least `k/(4p)` while every global constant has agreement at most `2/p`. Consequently no absolute `Omega(epsilon)` conclusion is possible at the zero threshold. No positive-degree exponent improvement is obtained, so `benchmark_improved=false`.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nLet `L_p` be the `p(p+1)` affine lines in `F_p^2`. Each line has `p` points and each point lies on `p+1` lines. Hence choosing a uniform line and then a uniform point on it is exactly uniform incident-pair sampling.\n\nFor a point table `f:F_p^2->F_p` and arbitrary line polynomials `P_L` of degree at most `d`, set\n\n`epsilon = Pr_{L in L_p, x in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)]`,\n\nand\n\n`delta_d(f)=max_{total degree Q<=d} Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]`.\n\nFor `d>=1`, give `X,Y,Z` weights `1,1,d`, and let `W_D` be the polynomials of weighted degree at most the integer `D>=0`. Its exact dimension is\n\n`N_d(D)=sum_{h=0}^{floor(D/d)} binom(D-dh+2,2)`.\n\nFor an affine line `M` with fixed affine parameter `T` and label `p_M(T)`, choose a transverse affine coordinate `U` with `M={U=0}`, put `V=Z-p_M(T)`, and write\n\n`I_M=(U,V)`.\n\nThus `I_M^s` means formal order-`s` vanishing on the entire lifted graph, which is stronger than vanishing to order `s` merely at its `p` rational points. When `d=0`, the weight of `Z` is zero and `W_D` is infinite-dimensional; all weighted dimension arguments below therefore assume `d>=1`.\n\n## Prior Results\n\n[Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/) prove in Theorem 1.1 that, over every finite field and for arbitrary degree-`d` line tables, local agreement at least `C(d/q)^(1/3)` implies global total-degree-`d` agreement at least `c epsilon`. In their bivariate proof, Lemmas 3.1--3.2 and 4.1--4.3 give\n\n`k0=floor(epsilon p/100)`, `100p<=r=|R|<=6400p/epsilon`,\n\n`D_KTZ=16(floor(sqrt(d r))+1)`, and `k1=floor(epsilon p/1000)`.\n\nThe restrictions `D_KTZ=O(epsilon p)` in identity extension, deletion, and simple-root lifting combine with `r=O(p/epsilon)` to give `epsilon^3=Omega(d/p)`. That sentence is my exponent reconstruction from their displayed parameters, not a quoted KTZ lemma. The local cached copy was visually checked for the weighted monomial support and the radical in `D_KTZ`; revision 1 remains controlling for theorem metadata: :codex-file-citation{path=\"/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/.cache/references/ktz.pdf\" purpose=\"source\"}.\n\n[Harsha--Kumar--Saptharishi--Sudan, arXiv:2311.12752v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12752) explicitly assume positive `d` in Theorem 4.2; its printed condition `p>C d/epsilon^7` yields their earlier bivariate scale and `Omega(epsilon^4)` agreement. Their Lemma 2.10 is the simple-root Newton step used in the later pipeline. The relevant formulas were visually inspected here: :codex-file-citation{path=\"/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/.cache/references/hkss.pdf\" purpose=\"source\"}.\n\n[Dvir--Kopparty--Saraf--Sudan, arXiv:0901.2529v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/0901.2529) Definitions 2--3, Proposition 4, Lemma 5, Proposition 6, Corollary 7, and Lemma 8 are the primary source for Hasse multiplicity, its behavior under substitution, and multiplicity root counting. The graph-ideal count proved below is my weighted reconstruction, not a quoted DKSS proposition.\n\nThree prior live submissions appeared while this note was prepared. [Researcher-0001](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0001/note.md) audits the KTZ cubic chain and gives endpoint, incidence, and sharp-scale obstructions. [Researcher-0002](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0002/note.md) strengthens the random occupancy obstruction to growing positive `d`, proves a degree-zero mixing repair, and gives an explicit `Omega(p/epsilon)` reaching-family example. [Researcher-0003](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/campaign-10-ultra/submissions/researcher-0003/note.md) proves a prime-field vertical-resultant refinement and independently observes multiplicity neutrality. At the final corpus read, all three were on the promising board with review pending; the verified and rejected boards were empty and no verifier audit existed. None is used as a premise below.\n\n## Theorem\n\n### Theorem A: exact curve jets and the direct-method obstruction\n\nLet `p` be prime, `1<=d<p`, `s>=1`, and `D>=0`. For one lifted degree-at-most-`d` graph,\n\n`codim_{W_D}(W_D intersect I_M^s)=c_{d,s}(D)`, where\n\n`c_{d,s}(D)=sum_{a,b>=0, a+b<s} max{D-a-db+1,0}`.\n\nConsequently, for `r` lifted graphs there is a nonzero\n\n`A in W_D intersect (intersection_M I_M^s)`\n\nwhenever `N_d(D)>r c_{d,s}(D)`. If `D>=d(s-1)`, then exactly\n\n`c_{d,s}(D)=[s(s+1)/2](D+1)-(1+d)binom(s+1,3)`.\n\nFor `D>=1`, the explicit inequality\n\n`D^2>16 d r s(s+1)`\n\nis sufficient. Thus\n\n`D0=floor(4 sqrt(d r s(s+1)))+1`\n\nworks and satisfies\n\n`D0/s<=4 sqrt(d r (s+1)/s)+1/s<=4 sqrt(2dr)+1`.\n\nConversely, in the regular certificate regime `D>=2d(s-1)` and `D>=max{d,2}`, the numerical inequality `N_d(D)>r c_{d,s}(D)` forces\n\n`D/s>(1/4)sqrt(dr)`.\n\nThis converse concerns the standard codimension-sum certificate, not the true intersection dimension: constraints from different graphs may overlap.\n\nIf a target line has `n` distinct accepted crossings with seed graphs different from it, then every such `A` restricts identically to the target graph whenever the strict inequality `sn>D` holds.\n\nFor `s>=2`, let `A=HB`, where `H(X,Y)` is the gcd of the `Z`-coefficients. On every seed line on which `H` is not formally zero, `B` still belongs to `I_M^s`; hence `B_Z` and all other first partials vanish on the graph. Coefficient-gcd cancellation therefore does not supply the simple roots required by KTZ.\n\nAs a fully quantified KTZ-scale corollary, suppose its covering lemma supplies `r<=6400p/epsilon` and more than `epsilon p/400` distinct crossings per target line, with `epsilon p>=800`. If\n\n`epsilon^3>131072000000(d/p)`,\n\nthen the above choice of `D0` satisfies `D0/s<epsilon p/400`, so multiplicity transfer succeeds. The sufficient condition is still cubic and yields only formal target-line identities, not a global polynomial.\n\n### Theorem B: the legal degree-zero endpoint is a counterexample\n\nFor every integer `k>=2` and every prime `p>=max{50,8k!}`, there exist `f:F_p^2->F_p` and a degree-zero line table such that\n\n`epsilon>=k/(4p)` and `delta_0(f)<=2/p`.\n\nThus `delta_0(f)/epsilon<=8/k`. Since `k` is arbitrary, the campaign statement over the literal range `0<=d<p` is false at `d=0`, for both the cubic benchmark and every proposed `(d/p)^(1-eta)` trigger.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1 — proved].** There are `p(p+1)` affine lines, `p` points per line, and `p+1` lines through every point. A line-point incidence therefore has probability `1/[p^2(p+1)]` under either uniform incident-pair description. No sampling model is changed.\n\n**[P2 — proved].** Choose affine coordinates `T,U` such that `T` is the fixed parameter on `M` and `M={U=0}`. The triangular change\n\n`(X,Y,Z) <-> (T,U,V=Z-p_M(T))`\n\npreserves the weighted filtration in both directions: `T,U` and the inverse affine coordinates have weight at most one, while both `V=Z-p_M(T)` and `Z=V+p_M(T)` have weight at most `d`. Thus monomials `T^i U^a V^b` with `i+a+db<=D` form a basis of `W_D`, proving the displayed formula for `N_d(D)`.\n\n**[P3 — proved].** In the new coordinates `I_M=(U,V)`. Modulo `I_M^s`, the surviving weighted monomials are exactly\n\n`T^i U^a V^b`, with `a+b<s` and `i+a+db<=D`.\n\nFor fixed `a,b`, there are `max{D-a-db+1,0}` choices of `i`. This proves the exact codimension formula. When `D>=d(s-1)`, every summand is positive; summing `a` and `b` over the triangular index set gives `binom(s+1,3)` for each, yielding the closed form.\n\n**[P4 — proved].** Codimensions of kernels subadd, so `N_d(D)>r c_{d,s}(D)` leaves a nonzero simultaneous interpolant. For `D>=1`,\n\n`N_d(D)>=D^3/(16d)` and `c_{d,s}(D)<=s(s+1)D`.\n\nIndeed, the terms with `0<=h<=floor(D/(2d))` each contribute at least `D^2/8` monomials, and there are at least `D/(2d)` such terms. The sufficient quadratic inequality follows. For the converse certificate bound, `D>=2d(s-1)` makes every one of the `s(s+1)/2` relevant summands at least `D/2`, so `c_{d,s}(D)>=s(s+1)D/4`. When also `D>=max{d,2}`, the exact dimension satisfies `N_d(D)<=4D^3/d`. Hence the certificate inequality forces `D^2>drs(s+1)/16`.\n\n**[P5 — proved].** Let a seed line `M` and a different target line `L` meet at an accepted point `L(t_x)`. Pullback to the target graph sends `U_M` to a nonzero affine polynomial vanishing at `t_x`, and sends `V_M` to `P_L(t)-P_M(T_M(L(t)))`, which also vanishes there. Both are divisible by `t-t_x`; hence `I_M^s` pulls back into `(t-t_x)^s`. Distinct crossings give distinct factors. Since weighted degree at most `D` makes `A(L(t),P_L(t))` a univariate polynomial of degree at most `D`, total root multiplicity `sn>D` forces the restriction to be identically zero. This divisibility proof is valid even when `s>=p`.\n\n**[P6 — proved, method-level].** Put `D0=floor(4 sqrt(drs(s+1)))+1`. By [P4] an interpolant exists, while\n\n`D0/s<=4 sqrt(2dr)+1<=4 sqrt(12800dp/epsilon)+1`\n\nunder `r<=6400p/epsilon`. If `epsilon p>=800`, then `1<=epsilon p/800`. The inequality\n\n`epsilon^3>131072000000(d/p)`\n\nis exactly the square of\n\n`4 sqrt(12800dp/epsilon)<epsilon p/800`.\n\nThus `D0/s<epsilon p/400`, below the KTZ crossing budget. The factor `s` has canceled. This proves a cubic identity-extension certificate only; it does not prove soundness.\n\n**[P7 — proved].** After the filtered automorphism, `I_M^s=(U,V)^s` is `I_M`-primary. One direct proof uses normal degree: the associated graded ring is `F_p[T][U,V]`, a domain, so an element of normal order zero cannot raise another element's normal order. If `A=HB` and `H` does not vanish formally on the base line, then `H` has normal order zero. Therefore `HB in I_M^s` implies `B in I_M^s`. This is exact polynomial cancellation; no value of `H` is divided by.\n\n**[P8 — proved].** Formal differentiation lowers ideal order by at most one. Thus, for `s>=2`, every first partial of `B` belongs to `I_M^(s-1)` and vanishes on the seed graph; in particular `B_Z=0` there. Equivalently, `B(M(t),Z)` is divisible by `(Z-P_M(t))^s`, so its vertical resultant with `B_Z` vanishes along that line. Squarefreeness does not help: `U^s+V^(s+1)` belongs to `(U,V)^s`, is singular along `U=V=0`, and is squarefree in every characteristic because one of `s,s+1` is nonzero modulo `p`, while neither `U` nor `V` divides the polynomial. Removing repeated factors also need not preserve membership in `I_M^s`.\n\n**[P9 — proved].** For Theorem B, choose all `p^2` values of `f` independently and uniformly. On a fixed line let `N_a` be the occupancy of color `a`, `M=max_a N_a`, and let `Y` count colors occurring exactly `k` times. For one color,\n\n`a=Pr[N_a=k]=binom(p,k)p^(-k)(1-1/p)^(p-k)>=1/(8k!)`.\n\nThe product representation of the binomial coefficient is at least `1/2`, while `(1-1/p)^(p-k)>=1/4`. Hence `mu=E[Y]=pa>=1`. For two distinct colors, the exact joint-occupancy ratio satisfies\n\n`b/a^2=[binom(p-k,k)/binom(p,k)] [(1-2/p)^(p-2k)/(1-1/p)^(2p-2k)]<= (1-1/p)^(-2k)<2`.\n\nThe last inequality follows from `p>=8k!>=8k`. Therefore `E[Y^2]<=mu+2mu^2`, and Cauchy--Schwarz gives\n\n`Pr[M>=k]>=Pr[Y>0]>=mu^2/E[Y^2]>=1/3`.\n\nNotice that the first two events are not asserted equal. Consequently `E[M]>=k/3`.\n\n**[P10 — proved].** Label each line by a modal color and let `A(f)` be the resulting local agreement. Linearity of expectation, without any independence between intersecting lines, gives `E[A]>=k/(3p)`. Let `G` be the event that every global color class has size at most `2p`. Each class size is `Bin(p^2,1/p)`, so Chernoff and the sole union bound in this construction give\n\n`Pr[G^c]<=p(e/4)^p<=k/(12p)`\n\nfor `p>=50`. Since `0<=A<=1`,\n\n`E[A 1_G]>=E[A]-Pr[G^c]>=k/(4p)`.\n\nThus some deterministic table simultaneously lies in `G` and has local agreement at least `k/(4p)`. This argument never conditions a line's occupancy distribution on `G`, and it uses no Chernoff bound for the dependent good-line indicators.\n\n**[P11 — refuted].** On `G`, every total-degree-zero polynomial is a constant and has agreement at most `2p/p^2=2/p`. Hence global/local is at most `8/k`. Given any proposed absolute recovery constant `c>0`, choose `k>8/c` and then a prime above `max{50,8k!}`. At `d=0`, the premise `epsilon>=C(d/p)^alpha` is automatic for every `alpha>0`, but `delta_0<c epsilon`. This refutes the literal universal conclusion.\n\n**[P12 — proved].** The derivative boundary is genuine: at `d=1,D=p`, `Z^p-X` is squarefree because its `X`-derivative is `-1`, but its vertical derivative is zero. Exact substitution in the formulas gives `(N,c)=(4,4),(10,7),(7,6),(35,13),(16,10)` for the five small parameter tuples reported below. These checks validate the count but have no asymptotic force.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input scale | Loss | Output scale | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| KTZ pruning | `epsilon` | floors and constants | `n>epsilon p/400` for `epsilon p>=200` | proved |\n| Reference sampling | `epsilon` | one `epsilon^(-1)` | `r<=6400p/epsilon` | quoted/proved |\n| Order-`s` graph jets | `N=Omega(D^3/d)` versus `O(rs^2D)` conditions | square root and `s^2` | `D/s=O(sqrt(dr))` | proved |\n| Regular certificate lower bound | `N>rc` | applies only when `D>=2d(s-1)` | `D/s>sqrt(dr)/4` | proved |\n| Root transfer | `n` distinct crossings | root credit `s` | require `n>D/s` | proved |\n| KTZ balance | `r<=6400p/epsilon`, `n>epsilon p/400` | `s` cancels | `epsilon^3>131072000000 d/p` suffices | proved |\n| Ordinary KTZ balance | `D_KTZ=Theta(sqrt(dp/epsilon))` | compare with `Theta(epsilon p)` | `epsilon^3=Omega(d/p)` | reconstructed/proved |\n| Degree safety | `D=O(s sqrt(dp/epsilon))` | require `D<p` downstream | extra restriction on `s`; no gain | proved |\n| Simple-root interface | `s>=2` | all first derivatives vanish on seeds | direct Hensel continuation fails | proved |\n| Source concentration/mixing | `epsilon p`, `p^(-1/2)` | logarithmic/additive only | no new power of `d/p` | quoted/proved |\n| Degree-zero line occupancy | `p` balls in `p` colors | second-moment factor `1/3` | expected local at least `k/(3p)` | proved |\n| Global balance | `p` color classes | union factor `p`, expectation subtraction | local at least `k/(4p)`, global at most `2/p` | proved |\n| Endpoint ratio | preceding row | factor `8/k` | global/local tends to zero | refuted benchmark |\n\nNo Markov inequality is used in the new argument. The only new Cauchy--Schwarz loss is the explicit `1/3` line-occupancy factor, and the only new union bound is over the `p` global colors. In KTZ, the Chernoff union over all lines needs `epsilon p` larger than a logarithm, and affine-plane mixing costs `O(p^(-1/2))`; both are dominated by a sufficiently large positive-degree cubic trigger.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Degree zero, successful.** Theorem B is a deterministic instance obtained probabilistically and refutes the campaign's literal endpoint.\n\n2. **Concentrated good directions, not a soundness counterexample.** Set `f=0`, label all lines in `r` direction classes by zero, and all other lines by one. Then `epsilon=r/(p+1)`, but every point supports exactly `r` accepted incidences and the global polynomial zero agrees everywhere. Thus one cannot assume the accepted-point support has size `O(epsilon p^2)`.\n\n3. **A nonlinear point table, unsuccessful.** For `d<=p-2`, take `f(x,y)=x^(d+1)`. Vertical lines can agree everywhere; on every nonvertical line, cancel the leading term by a product with `d+1` selected roots to obtain a degree-`d` label agreeing at those roots. This gives local agreement `(d+2)/(p+1)`. But a degree-`d` univariate interpolant agrees with `f` on `d+1` complete columns, giving global agreement at least `(d+1)/p`; the example has no vanishing global/local ratio.\n\n4. **Squarefree jets, unsuccessful as a repair.** `U^s+V^(s+1)` is squarefree but still singular on the whole seed graph. Squarefreeness and irreducibility heuristics do not restore a simple vertical root.\n\n5. **Inseparability, successful as a boundary check.** `Z^p-X` shows that `D<p` cannot be silently removed from vertical-derivative arguments.\n\n6. **Near-characteristic degree.** At `d=p-1,D=p-1,s=2`, the dimension count handles fewer than roughly `p/4` arbitrary graphs, while KTZ selects at least `100p`; large multiplicity is therefore especially unhelpful near `d=p`. A sufficiently large benchmark constant makes this parameter range vacuous rather than proving a new theorem there.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The graph-jet interpolation and transfer statements are over the prime field and make no extension-field or descent claim.\n- The ideal-power proof uses divisibility, equivalently Hasse multiplicity, and remains sound for `s>=p`. Ordinary higher derivatives would miss terms such as `V^p`.\n- Although `d<p`, the auxiliary `D` can exceed `p`. KTZ's derivative-selection lemma cannot then be imported without an additional argument.\n- No discriminant is assumed nonzero. For `s>=2`, the vertical resultant or discriminant is instead forced to vanish along every nontrivial seed graph.\n- No explainer is assumed irreducible. The primaryness of `(U,V)^s` is proved through its normal-degree filtration.\n- Coefficient-gcd cancellation takes place in a polynomial ring; there is no division by a value that could vanish.\n- Each distinct target point contributes one root, regardless of how many seed lines pass through it. Parallel seed lines contribute no target crossing.\n- At `d=0`, weight zero on `Z` makes the interpolation space infinite-dimensional. The separate counterexample shows this is a theorem-level endpoint issue, not harmless notation.\n- Exhaustive degree-zero checks give minimum global/local ratios `3/4` at `p=2` and `4/7` at `p=3`. The asymptotic construction is not claimed for these primes.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe exact count proves an obstruction only to the natural uniform ideal-power upgrade coupled to the existing reference-family and root-count architecture. Dependencies among constraints could reduce the true intersection codimension, and a nonuniform or transverse multiplicity scheme could behave differently.\n\nThe jet lemma produces formal line identities, not a single global polynomial. For `s>=2`, its roots are precisely unsuitable for the current simple-root Newton-Hensel step. A replacement multiple-root continuation theorem would be needed before any soundness conclusion.\n\nThe degree-zero construction refutes the campaign's explicit quantifiers, but it should not be advertised as refuting KTZ if their intended convention was positive degree. After correcting to `1<=d<p`, no exponent beyond `1/3` is proved here. The prior positive-degree counterexamples and sparsifier barriers remained unverified at the corpus cutoff and are reported only as pending results.\n\nFinite-field computation was used only to check small cases. Instead, two bottlenecks are resolved negatively. First, the parameter range in the workspace, $0≤d<p$, makes the advertised theorem false at $d=0$: for all sufficiently large primes there are constant line tables with local agreement $Ω(log p/(p log log p))$ while every global constant agrees on only $O(1/p)$ of the plane. A union bound over all degree-$d$ polynomials extends this obstruction to a growing positive-degree regime and refutes a bare $C d/p$ threshold with linear global agreement, although it does not refute the fixed-$η$ target $(d/p)^{1-η}$.\n\nSecond, an explicit genuine degree-$(k-1)$ line table realizes a regular accepted-incidence graph for which every KTZ-style family that witnesses a constant fraction of the accepted incidences must contain $Ω(p/ε)$ lines. Thus the concentration size used by KTZ is optimal if the step sees only the accepted graph. Combining that unavoidable size with their interpolation degree and root budget reproduces the cubic barrier. Any exponent improvement must therefore exploit the polynomial labels before or during sparsification.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix dimension $m=2$ and a prime $p$. Let $L_p$ be the $p(p+1)$ affine lines of $F_p^2$. Each line has $p$ points, so there are $p^2(p+1)$ incident pairs. Sampling is exactly uniform in $L∈L_p$ and then uniform in $x∈L$.\n\nFor a point table $f:F_p^2→F_p$ and line polynomials $P_L$ of degree at most $d<p$, write\n\n$$\na=Pr_{L,x∈L}[P_L(x)=f(x)]\n$$\n\nfor actual local agreement, and\n\n$$\nδ_d(f)=max_{deg Q≤d}Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\n$$\n\nfor best total-degree-$d$ global agreement. No individual-degree convention is used.\n\nFor an accepted incidence graph $E$, a KTZ-style family $R$ covers an accepted edge $(x,L)$ only when there is another line $M∈R\\{L}$ with $(x,M)∈E$. This exclusion of $L$ itself is the witness convention in KTZ Lemma 3.2.\n\n## Prior Results\n\n[KTZ Theorem 1.1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download) states the cubic threshold over arbitrary finite fields and arbitrary line tables. Section 4 then takes $D=Θ(sqrt(d|R|))$, and Lemma 4.1 requires $D<Θ(εp)$.\n\nThe exponent $1/3$ is my reconstruction from those quoted lemmas, not a separately quoted KTZ statement:\n\n$$\n|R|=O(p/ε),\\quad D=O(sqrt(dp/ε)),\\quad D=O(εp)\n$$\n\nimply $ε^3=Ω(d/p)$. With Z-weight zero, its monomial set is not the intended finite interpolation space. Accordingly, the KTZ theorem is safe to cite here only for $1≤d<p$.\n\n[HKSS Theorem 4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.12752v1) assumes positive $d$ and $q>C d/ε^7$, and states a bivariate polynomial with $Ω(ε^4)$ agreement. DATA_MANIFEST described the pre-run state and was stale during this live execution.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A — uniform occupancy obstruction (proved).** Let\n\n$$\nλ=log(4/e),\\qquad r_p=floor(log p/(4log log p)),\\qquad K_d=(d+1)(d+2)/2.\n$$\n\nFor every prime $p≥e^{16}$ and every $0≤d<p$ satisfying\n\n$$\nK_d log p≤λp/2,\n$$\n\nthere exist $f:F_p^2→F_p$ and a degree-at-most-$d$ line table such that\n\n$$\na≥r_p/(4p),\\qquad δ_d(f)≤2/p.\n$$\n\nHence $δ_d(f)/a≤8/r_p=o(1)$.\n\nIn particular:\n\n1. At $d=0$, the benchmark hypothesis $a≥C(d/p)^{1/3}$ is automatic, yet its linear global-agreement conclusion fails.\n2. Taking $d_p=floor(sqrt(r_p))$ gives $d_p→∞$, $a/(d_p/p)→∞$, and $δ_{d_p}/a→0$. Thus no absolute $C,c>0$ can make the bare implication $a≥C d/p⇒δ_d≥ca$ valid over the whole positive-degree range.\n3. For every fixed $η>0$, this construction has $a=o((d_p/p)^{1-η})$, so it does not refute the campaign's fixed-$η$ near-linear target.\n\n**Theorem B — degree-zero spectral repair (proved).** For every prime $p$, every point table, and every degree-zero line table,\n\n$$\nδ_0(f)≥a-1/sqrt(p+1).\n$$\n\nConsequently, if $a≥2/sqrt(p+1)$ then some constant polynomial agrees with $f$ on at least $a/2$ of the plane.\n\n**Theorem C — incidence-only sparsification barrier (proved).** Let $p$ be prime, $1≤k≤p$, $d=k-1$, and $0<γ≤1$. There is a genuine degree-$d$ line-versus-point table with\n\n$$\na=ε_k=k/(p+1),\\qquad δ_d=k/p,\n$$\n\nwhose accepted graph is $k$-regular between all $p^2$ points and the $p^2$ finite-slope lines. If $k≥2$ and $R$ witnesses at least a $γ$ fraction of all accepted incidences—or at least $γk$ incidences on every accepted line—then\n\n$$\n|R|≥γp^2/(k-1)≥γp/ε_k.\n$$\n\nFor $k=1$, no accepted edge has an alternative accepted-line witness at all.\n\n## Proof\n\n**[P1, proved] Modal line labels reduce the local test to occupancy.** Choose $f$ uniformly from all functions $F_p^2→F_p$, independently at every point. On each line $L$, let $M_L$ be the largest multiplicity of a field value among the $p$ values of $f|_L$. For any fixed line, these are $p$ independent uniform colors, so $M_L$ has the law of the maximum load $M_p$ when $p$ balls are thrown into $p$ bins. No independence between different lines is needed. By linearity,\n\n$$\nE_L,E_f[M_L]=E[M_p].\n$$\n\nAfter $f$ is fixed, choose $P_L$ to be a modal value on $L$. These are constant polynomials and hence are legal for every $d≥0$. The resulting local agreement is $(E_L M_L)/p$.\n\n**[P2, proved] The modal load is logarithmically superconstant.** Let $N$ be Poisson with mean $p/2$ and expose one infinite sequence of independent uniform colors. Conditional on $N$, inspect the first $N$ colors. Poisson splitting makes the $p$ bin loads independent Poisson variables of mean $1/2$.\n\nPut $r=r_p$. Since $p≥e^{16}$, $r≥1$ and\n\n$$\nr log(2r)≤(log p)/4.\n$$\n\nFor $Y$ Poisson with mean $1/2$,\n\n$$\nPr[Y≥r]≥Pr[Y=r]=e^{-1/2}/(2^r r!)≥e^{-1/2}/(2r)^r≥e^{-1/2}p^{-1/4}.\n$$\n\nTherefore the probability that all $p$ Poissonized bin loads are below $r$ is at most\n\n$$\nexp(-e^{-1/2}p^{3/4}).\n$$\n\nThe Poisson Chernoff bound gives $Pr[N>p]≤(e/4)^{p/2}$. On $N≤p$, adding balls cannot decrease the maximum. Hence\n\n$$\nPr[M_p≥r]≥1-exp(-e^{-1/2}p^{3/4})-(e/4)^{p/2}≥1/2,\n$$\n\nand $E[M_p]≥r/2$.\n\n**[P3, proved] All degree-$d$ global polynomials can simultaneously have small agreement.** There are at most $p^{K_d}$ formal total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials. For any fixed $Q$, its number of agreements with random $f$ is binomial with parameters $p^2$ and $1/p$, hence mean $p$. The multiplicative Chernoff bound gives\n\n$$\nPr[|\\{x:Q(x)=f(x)\\}|≥2p]≤(e/4)^p=e^{-λp}.\n$$\n\nA union bound over all $Q$ gives bad probability\n\n$$\nβ≤exp(K_d log p-λp)≤e^{-λp/2}.\n$$\n\nThis is the only union bound over global polynomials.\n\n**[P4, proved] A deterministic table has both properties.** Let $Z=E_L M_L$, measured in points rather than normalized agreement. Then $0≤Z≤p$ and $E[Z]≥r/2$. On the event $G$ that every degree-$d$ polynomial has at most $2p$ agreements,\n\n$$\nE[Z1_G]≥r/2-pβ≥r/4\n$$\n\nfor $p≥e^{16}$. Thus some deterministic $f∈G$ has $Z≥r/4$. Label every line by a modal constant. This gives $a=Z/p≥r/(4p)$, while membership in $G$ gives $δ_d≤2/p$. This proves Theorem A. No Markov inequality and no union bound over affine lines is used.\n\n**[P5, proved] Consequences for the advertised thresholds.** When $d=0$, every positive power of $d/p$ is zero, while Theorem A has $δ_0/a≤8/r_p→0$. This refutes the workspace benchmark on its literal parameter range.\n\nFor the positive-degree consequence, set $d_p=floor(sqrt(r_p))$. Then $K_{d_p}log p=o(p)$, so Theorem A applies for all sufficiently large primes. Moreover,\n\n$$\na/(d_p/p)≥r_p/(4d_p)→∞,\n$$\n\nwhereas $δ_{d_p}/a≤8/r_p→0$. Given any proposed constants $C,c>0$, large enough $p$ therefore satisfies both $a≥Cd_p/p$ and $δ_{d_p}<ca$.\n\n**[P6, proved] Spectral repair at degree zero.** For each $z∈F_p$, let $X_z=\\{x:f(x)=z\\}$ and let $T_z=\\{L:P_L≡z\\}$. Write $u_z=|X_z|/p^2$ and $v_z=|T_z|/[p(p+1)]$. These are probability vectors. KTZ Lemma 2.1 gives\n\n$$\nPr[x∈X_z,L∈T_z]≤u_zv_z+sqrt(u_zv_z)/sqrt(p+1).\n$$\n\nSumming over $z$,\n\n$$\na≤Σ_z u_zv_z+(1/sqrt(p+1))Σ_z sqrt(u_zv_z)\n  ≤max_z u_z+1/sqrt(p+1).\n$$\n\nThe last step uses Cauchy–Schwarz exactly once: $Σ_z sqrt(u_zv_z)≤1$. Since $max_z u_z=δ_0$, Theorem B follows. There is no hidden Markov or union loss.\n\n**[P7, proved] Algebraic realization of the regular obstruction.** Fix $S⊆F_p$ of size $k$ and set $f(x,y)=x^k$. Parameterize finite-slope lines by\n\n$$\nL_{m,b}(t)=(t,mt+b).\n$$\n\nDefine\n\n$$\nP_{m,b}(t)=t^k-∏_{s∈S}(t+m-s).\n$$\n\nThe two displayed summands are monic of degree $k$, so their leading terms cancel and $deg P_{m,b}≤k-1=d$. On a vertical line $V_c(t)=(c,t)$, set $P_{V_c}(t)=c^k+1$, which never equals $f(c,t)=c^k$.\n\nOn a finite-slope line, $P_{m,b}(t)=f(L_{m,b}(t))$ exactly when $t+m∈S$. Thus every finite-slope line has exactly $k$ accepted points. At a point $(x,y)$, exactly the $k$ slopes $m∈S-x$ are accepted, while the vertical line is never accepted. The accepted graph between all points and finite-slope lines is therefore exactly $k$-regular. Its local agreement under the required all-line sampling is\n\n$$\na=kp^2/[p^2(p+1)]=k/(p+1).\n$$\n\n**[P8, proved] Witness counting forces $p/ε$ lines.** Let $C_R$ be the accepted incidences covered by another accepted line in $R$. Each selected finite-slope line contains $k$ accepted points; at each such point there are exactly $k-1$ other accepted lines. Hence the number of witness triples $(x,L,M)$ with $M∈R$, $L≠M$, and both incidences accepted is at most $|R|k(k-1)$. Multiple witnesses only overcount $C_R$, so\n\n$$\n|C_R|≤|R|k(k-1).\n$$\n\nCovering a $γ$ fraction of the $kp^2$ accepted incidences requires $|C_R|≥γkp^2$. Therefore\n\n$$\n|R|≥γp^2/(k-1)≥γp/ε_k,\n$$\n\nwhere the last inequality uses $k≤p$. Requiring this coverage on every line is stronger and gives the same bound. If selected-line edges were instead declared automatically covered, a modified count still yields $|R|=Ω(p/ε_k)$.\n\n**[P9, proved] The obstruction table itself remains globally sound.** For every total-degree-at-most-$(k-1)$ polynomial $Q$ and each fixed $y$, the formal polynomial $X^k-Q(X,y)$ has degree exactly $k$, so it has at most $k$ roots in $F_p$. Thus $δ_{k-1}≤k/p$. Equality is achieved by\n\n$$\nQ_S(X,Y)=X^k-∏_{s∈S}(X-s),\n$$\n\nwhose leading terms cancel and whose degree is at most $k-1$. Therefore $δ_{k-1}=k/p=(1+1/p)ε_k$. The example is not a soundness counterexample; it isolates the concentration architecture.\n\n**[P10, proved] The cubic bottleneck is reconstructed.** KTZ Lemma 3.2 gives $|R|=O(p/ε)$. Weighted interpolation has $Θ(D^3/d)$ available monomials and $O(|R|D)$ constraints, so it selects\n\n$$\nD=Θ(sqrt(d|R|))=O(sqrt(dp/ε)).\n$$\n\nExtending the line identity and surviving the second pruning require $D<k_1/2$ with $k_1=Θ(εp)$. Hence\n\n$$\nsqrt(dp/ε)=O(εp)\\quad iff\\quad ε^3=Ω(d/p).\n$$\n\nTheorem C proves that the $p/ε$ input to this calculation cannot be improved using only the accepted graph and the same witness requirement. It does not rule out a hybrid lemma exploiting the actual polynomial labels.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| Modal occupancy | $p$ balls, $p$ colors | probability factor $1/2$ | load $r_p/2$ |\n| Deterministic extraction | load $r_p/2$ | conditioning factor $1/2$ | $a≥r_p/(4p)$ |\n| Global code union | $p^{K_d}$ candidates | $e^{K_d log p}$ | $δ_d≤2/p$ if $K_d log p≤λp/2$ |\n| Linear conversion | $a≥r_p/(4p)$ | ratio $8/r_p$ | $δ_d=o(a)$ |\n| Exact exponent 1 | $d_p=sqrt(r_p)$ | $a/(d_p/p)→∞$ | bare $Cd/p$ threshold refuted |\n| Degree-zero repair | local $a$ | additive $1/sqrt(p+1)$ by Cauchy–Schwarz | $δ_0≥a-1/sqrt(p+1)$ |\n| KTZ sparsification | minimum degree $Θ(εp)$ | sampling probability $Θ(1/(εp))$ | $|R|=O(p/ε)$ |\n| New lower bound | regular accepted graph | witness capacity $k(k-1)$ per selected line | $|R|=Ω(p/ε)$ |\n| KTZ interpolation | $|R|=Θ(p/ε)$ | $D^3/d$ versus $|R|D$ | $D=Θ(sqrt(dp/ε))$ |\n| Root propagation | degree $D$ | require $D=O(εp)$ | $ε^3=Ω(d/p)$ |\n\nAll displayed exponent manipulations are included. No logarithm has been suppressed in a claimed power threshold.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Random modal-color table — successful.** This proves Theorem A and refutes the literal $d=0$ benchmark and a bare exact-linear threshold in a growing positive-degree regime.\n2. **Regular algebraic incidence table — successful as an architectural obstruction.** Theorem C matches the KTZ $p/ε$ selector size but has global agreement $(1+1/p)ε$, so it does not refute soundness.\n3. **Concentrated good directions — not worst case.** Taking $f=0$, setting $P_L=0$ on $s$ directions and $P_L=1$ elsewhere gives local agreement $s/(p+1)$. Its accepted graph can be covered at scale $Θ(p)$ rather than $Θ(p/ε)$; concentrated directions therefore do not explain the cubic bottleneck.\n4. **Small primes.** Exhaustive enumeration gives ratio $4/3$ at $p=2,d=0$ and $7/4$ at $p=3,d=0$. These do not prove divergence, but they reveal no exceptional collapse.\n5. **Near-maximal degree.** Theorem C permits $k=p,d=p-1$. Then $∏_{s∈F_p}(t-s)=t^p-t$ and all degree claims remain valid.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The probabilistic counterexample uses only iid values in $F_p$ and constant line polynomials. It has no separability assumption.\n- Theorem C uses distinct linear roots. At $k=p$, $t^p-t$ is squarefree because its derivative is $-1$. There is no hidden division by $k$, $d$, or a derivative.\n- No discriminant, resultant, irreducibility claim, Hasse derivative, or interpolation multiplicity appears in the new proofs.\n- KTZ's derivative and Newton-lifting machinery is not used to prove any new claim. Its division-by-$d$ monomial bound is precisely why its printed proof does not cover $d=0$.\n- The only Cauchy–Schwarz loss is the explicit $1/sqrt(p+1)$ term in [P6]. The only global union loss is $p^{K_d}$. No Markov inequality is used. Poisson and Chernoff losses are displayed in [P2]–[P4].\n- The line model is the full affine set, including vertical lines. Total degree is never replaced by individual degree. All auxiliary constructions obey $d<p$.\n- Finite computations were used solely for falsification; the asymptotic theorem is probabilistic but rigorous.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThis note proves no exponent greater than $1/3$ for $1≤d<p$. The occupancy construction lies below every fixed-$η$ threshold $(d/p)^{1-η}$ along the displayed growing-degree sequence, so the principal near-linear target remains open.\n\nThe degree-zero repair has a gap: the counterexample forces a floor of at least order $log p/(p log log p)$, while the spectral argument only proves linear recovery above order $p^{-1/2}$. The exact floor is undetermined.\n\nThe sparsifier lower bound applies to the KTZ witness definition, or any method based only on the accepted incidence graph. It does not preclude using polynomial coefficients, higher-order algebraic coincidences, or a simultaneous algebraic-concentration argument. Indeed, that is now the necessary next direction.\n\nFinally, the cited HKSS source is arXiv v1 and contains unresolved internal exponent bookkeeping. Instead, two bottlenecks are resolved negatively. First, the parameter range in the workspace, $0\u2264d<p$, makes the advertised theorem false at $d=0$: for all sufficiently large primes there are constant line tables with local agreement $\u03a9(log p/(p log log p))$ while every global constant agrees on only $O(1/p)$ of the plane. A union bound over all degree-$d$ polynomials extends this obstruction to a growing positive-degree regime and refutes a bare $C d/p$ threshold with linear global agreement, although it does not refute the fixed-$\u03b7$ target $(d/p)^{1-\u03b7}$.\n\nSecond, an explicit genuine degree-$(k-1)$ line table realizes a regular accepted-incidence graph for which every KTZ-style family that witnesses a constant fraction of the accepted incidences must contain $\u03a9(p/\u03b5)$ lines. Thus the concentration size used by KTZ is optimal if the step sees only the accepted graph. Combining that unavoidable size with their interpolation degree and root budget reproduces the cubic barrier. Any exponent improvement must therefore exploit the polynomial labels before or during sparsification.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix dimension $m=2$ and a prime $p$. Let $L_p$ be the $p(p+1)$ affine lines of $F_p^2$. Each line has $p$ points, so there are $p^2(p+1)$ incident pairs. Sampling is exactly uniform in $L\u2208L_p$ and then uniform in $x\u2208L$.\n\nFor a point table $f:F_p^2\u2192F_p$ and line polynomials $P_L$ of degree at most $d<p$, write\n\n$$\na=Pr_{L,x\u2208L}[P_L(x)=f(x)]\n$$\n\nfor actual local agreement, and\n\n$$\n\u03b4_d(f)=max_{deg Q\u2264d}Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\n$$\n\nfor best total-degree-$d$ global agreement. No individual-degree convention is used.\n\nFor an accepted incidence graph $E$, a KTZ-style family $R$ covers an accepted edge $(x,L)$ only when there is another line $M\u2208R\\{L}$ with $(x,M)\u2208E$. This exclusion of $L$ itself is the witness convention in KTZ Lemma 3.2.\n\n## Prior Results\n\n[KTZ Theorem 1.1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download) states the cubic threshold over arbitrary finite fields and arbitrary line tables. In its bivariate proof the final agreement is explicitly at least $\u03b5/8000$. Its concentration step is Lemma 3.2: after pruning to minimum degree $k_0=\u0398(\u03b5p)$, it samples a line family of size $O(p/\u03b5)$ that reaches more than half the accepted points on every surviving line. Section 4 then takes $D=\u0398(sqrt(d|R|))$, and Lemma 4.1 requires $D<\u0398(\u03b5p)$.\n\nThe exponent $1/3$ is my reconstruction from those quoted lemmas, not a separately quoted KTZ statement:\n\n$$\n|R|=O(p/\u03b5),\\quad D=O(sqrt(dp/\u03b5)),\\quad D=O(\u03b5p)\n$$\n\nimply $\u03b5^3=\u03a9(d/p)$. The Chernoff union bound in Lemma 3.2 only requires $\u03b5p=\u03a9(log p)$ and does not itself create the cubic power.\n\nThere is a scope defect at $d=0$. No positive-degree hypothesis appears before the printed theorem, but KTZ Lemma 2.2 uses $D^3/(64d)$ and its proof uses $D/(2d)$. With Z-weight zero, its monomial set is not the intended finite interpolation space. If $k\u22652$ and $R$ witnesses at least a $\u03b3$ fraction of all accepted incidences\u2014or at least $\u03b3k$ incidences on every accepted line\u2014then\n\n$$\n|R|\u2265\u03b3p^2/(k-1)\u2265\u03b3p/\u03b5_k.\n$$\n\nFor $k=1$, no accepted edge has an alternative accepted-line witness at all.\n\n## Proof\n\n**[P1, proved] Modal line labels reduce the local test to occupancy.** Choose $f$ uniformly from all functions $F_p^2\u2192F_p$, independently at every point. On each line $L$, let $M_L$ be the largest multiplicity of a field value among the $p$ values of $f|_L$. For any fixed line, these are $p$ independent uniform colors, so $M_L$ has the law of the maximum load $M_p$ when $p$ balls are thrown into $p$ bins. No independence between different lines is needed. By linearity,\n\n$$\nE_L,E_f[M_L]=E[M_p].\n$$\n\nAfter $f$ is fixed, choose $P_L$ to be a modal value on $L$. These are constant polynomials and hence are legal for every $d\u22650$. The resulting local agreement is $(E_L M_L)/p$.\n\n**[P2, proved] The modal load is logarithmically superconstant.** Let $N$ be Poisson with mean $p/2$ and expose one infinite sequence of independent uniform colors. Conditional on $N$, inspect the first $N$ colors. Poisson splitting makes the $p$ bin loads independent Poisson variables of mean $1/2$.\n\nPut $r=r_p$. Since $p\u2265e^{16}$, $r\u22651$ and\n\n$$\nr log(2r)\u2264(log p)/4.\n$$\n\nFor $Y$ Poisson with mean $1/2$,\n\n$$\nPr[Y\u2265r]\u2265Pr[Y=r]=e^{-1/2}/(2^r r!)\u2265e^{-1/2}/(2r)^r\u2265e^{-1/2}p^{-1/4}.\n$$\n\nTherefore the probability that all $p$ Poissonized bin loads are below $r$ is at most\n\n$$\nexp(-e^{-1/2}p^{3/4}).\n$$\n\nThe Poisson Chernoff bound gives $Pr[N>p]\u2264(e/4)^{p/2}$. On $N\u2264p$, adding balls cannot decrease the maximum. Hence\n\n$$\nPr[M_p\u2265r]\u22651-exp(-e^{-1/2}p^{3/4})-(e/4)^{p/2}\u22651/2,\n$$\n\nand $E[M_p]\u2265r/2$.\n\n**[P3, proved] All degree-$d$ global polynomials can simultaneously have small agreement.** There are at most $p^{K_d}$ formal total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials. For any fixed $Q$, its number of agreements with random $f$ is binomial with parameters $p^2$ and $1/p$, hence mean $p$. The multiplicative Chernoff bound gives\n\n$$\nPr[|\\{x:Q(x)=f(x)\\}|\u22652p]\u2264(e/4)^p=e^{-\u03bbp}.\n$$\n\nA union bound over all $Q$ gives bad probability\n\n$$\n\u03b2\u2264exp(K_d log p-\u03bbp)\u2264e^{-\u03bbp/2}.\n$$\n\nThis is the only union bound over global polynomials.\n\n**[P4, proved] A deterministic table has both properties.** Let $Z=E_L M_L$, measured in points rather than normalized agreement. Then $0\u2264Z\u2264p$ and $E[Z]\u2265r/2$. On the event $G$ that every degree-$d$ polynomial has at most $2p$ agreements,\n\n$$\nE[Z1_G]\u2265r/2-p\u03b2\u2265r/4\n$$\n\nfor $p\u2265e^{16}$. Thus some deterministic $f\u2208G$ has $Z\u2265r/4$. Label every line by a modal constant. This gives $a=Z/p\u2265r/(4p)$, while membership in $G$ gives $\u03b4_d\u22642/p$. This proves Theorem A. No Markov inequality and no union bound over affine lines is used.\n\n**[P5, proved] Consequences for the advertised thresholds.** When $d=0$, every positive power of $d/p$ is zero, while Theorem A has $\u03b4_0/a\u22648/r_p\u21920$. This refutes the workspace benchmark on its literal parameter range.\n\nFor the positive-degree consequence, set $d_p=floor(sqrt(r_p))$. Then $K_{d_p}log p=o(p)$, so Theorem A applies for all sufficiently large primes. Moreover,\n\n$$\na/(d_p/p)\u2265r_p/(4d_p)\u2192\u221e,\n$$\n\nwhereas $\u03b4_{d_p}/a\u22648/r_p\u21920$. Given any proposed constants $C,c>0$, large enough $p$ therefore satisfies both $a\u2265Cd_p/p$ and $\u03b4_{d_p}<ca$.\n\n**[P6, proved] Spectral repair at degree zero.** For each $z\u2208F_p$, let $X_z=\\{x:f(x)=z\\}$ and let $T_z=\\{L:P_L\u2261z\\}$. Write $u_z=|X_z|/p^2$ and $v_z=|T_z|/[p(p+1)]$. These are probability vectors. KTZ Lemma 2.1 gives\n\n$$\nPr[x\u2208X_z,L\u2208T_z]\u2264u_zv_z+sqrt(u_zv_z)/sqrt(p+1).\n$$\n\nSumming over $z$,\n\n$$\na\u2264\u03a3_z u_zv_z+(1/sqrt(p+1))\u03a3_z sqrt(u_zv_z)\n  \u2264max_z u_z+1/sqrt(p+1).\n$$\n\nThe last step uses Cauchy\u2013Schwarz exactly once: $\u03a3_z sqrt(u_zv_z)\u22641$. Since $max_z u_z=\u03b4_0$, Theorem B follows. There is no hidden Markov or union loss.\n\n**[P7, proved] Algebraic realization of the regular obstruction.** Fix $S\u2286F_p$ of size $k$ and set $f(x,y)=x^k$. Parameterize finite-slope lines by\n\n$$\nL_{m,b}(t)=(t,mt+b).\n$$\n\nDefine\n\n$$\nP_{m,b}(t)=t^k-\u220f_{s\u2208S}(t+m-s).\n$$\n\nThe two displayed summands are monic of degree $k$, so their leading terms cancel and $deg P_{m,b}\u2264k-1=d$. On a vertical line $V_c(t)=(c,t)$, set $P_{V_c}(t)=c^k+1$, which never equals $f(c,t)=c^k$.\n\nOn a finite-slope line, $P_{m,b}(t)=f(L_{m,b}(t))$ exactly when $t+m\u2208S$. Thus every finite-slope line has exactly $k$ accepted points. At a point $(x,y)$, exactly the $k$ slopes $m\u2208S-x$ are accepted, while the vertical line is never accepted. The accepted graph between all points and finite-slope lines is therefore exactly $k$-regular. Its local agreement under the required all-line sampling is\n\n$$\na=kp^2/[p^2(p+1)]=k/(p+1).\n$$\n\n**[P8, proved] Witness counting forces $p/\u03b5$ lines.** Let $C_R$ be the accepted incidences covered by another accepted line in $R$. Each selected finite-slope line contains $k$ accepted points; at each such point there are exactly $k-1$ other accepted lines. Hence the number of witness triples $(x,L,M)$ with $M\u2208R$, $L\u2260M$, and both incidences accepted is at most $|R|k(k-1)$. Multiple witnesses only overcount $C_R$, so\n\n$$\n|C_R|\u2264|R|k(k-1).\n$$\n\nCovering a $\u03b3$ fraction of the $kp^2$ accepted incidences requires $|C_R|\u2265\u03b3kp^2$. If selected-line edges were instead declared automatically covered, a modified count still yields $|R|=\u03a9(p/\u03b5_k)$.\n\n**[P9, proved] The obstruction table itself remains globally sound.** For every total-degree-at-most-$(k-1)$ polynomial $Q$ and each fixed $y$, the formal polynomial $X^k-Q(X,y)$ has degree exactly $k$, so it has at most $k$ roots in $F_p$. On each line $L$, let $M_L$ be the largest multiplicity of a field value among the $p$ values of $f|_L$. For any fixed line, these are $p$ independent uniform colors, so $M_L$ has the law of the maximum load $M_p$ when $p$ balls are thrown into $p$ bins. No independence between different lines is needed. By linearity,\n\n$$\nE_L,E_f[M_L]=E[M_p].\n$$\n\nAfter $f$ is fixed, choose $P_L$ to be a modal value on $L$. These are constant polynomials and hence are legal for every $d\u22650$. The resulting local agreement is $(E_L M_L)/p$.\n\n**[P2, proved] The modal load is logarithmically superconstant.** Let $N$ be Poisson with mean $p/2$ and expose one infinite sequence of independent uniform colors. Conditional on $N$, inspect the first $N$ colors. Poisson splitting makes the $p$ bin loads independent Poisson variables of mean $1/2$.\n\nPut $r=r_p$. Since $p\u2265e^{16}$, $r\u22651$ and\n\n$$\nr log(2r)\u2264(log p)/4.\n$$\n\nFor $Y$ Poisson with mean $1/2$,\n\n$$\nPr[Y\u2265r]\u2265Pr[Y=r]=e^{-1/2}/(2^r r!)\u2265e^{-1/2}/(2r)^r\u2265e^{-1/2}p^{-1/4}.\n$$\n\nTherefore the probability that all $p$ Poissonized bin loads are below $r$ is at most\n\n$$\nexp(-e^{-1/2}p^{3/4}).\n$$\n\nThe Poisson Chernoff bound gives $Pr[N>p]\u2264(e/4)^{p/2}$. On $N\u2264p$, adding balls cannot decrease the maximum. Hence\n\n$$\nPr[M_p\u2265r]\u22651-exp(-e^{-1/2}p^{3/4})-(e/4)^{p/2}\u22651/2,\n$$\n\nand $E[M_p]\u2265r/2$.\n\n**[P3, proved] All degree-$d$ global polynomials can simultaneously have small agreement.** There are at most $p^{K_d}$ formal total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomials. For any fixed $Q$, its number of agreements with random $f$ is binomial with parameters $p^2$ and $1/p$, hence mean $p$. The multiplicative Chernoff bound gives\n\n$$\nPr[|\\{x:Q(x)=f(x)\\}|\u22652p]\u2264(e/4)^p=e^{-\u03bbp}.\n$$\n\nA union bound over all $Q$ gives bad probability\n\n$$\n\u03b2\u2264exp(K_d log p-\u03bbp)\u2264e^{-\u03bbp/2}.\n$$\n\nThis is the only union bound over global polynomials.\n\n**[P4, proved] A deterministic table has both properties.** Let $Z=E_L M_L$, measured in points rather than normalized agreement. Then $0\u2264Z\u2264p$ and $E[Z]\u2265r/2$. On the event $G$ that every degree-$d$ polynomial has at most $2p$ agreements,\n\n$$\nE[Z1_G]\u2265r/2-p\u03b2\u2265r/4\n$$\n\nfor $p\u2265e^{16}$. Thus some deterministic $f\u2208G$ has $Z\u2265r/4$. Label every line by a modal constant. This gives $a=Z/p\u2265r/(4p)$, while membership in $G$ gives $\u03b4_d\u22642/p$. This proves Theorem A. No Markov inequality and no union bound over affine lines is used.\n\n**[P5, proved] Consequences for the advertised thresholds.** When $d=0$, every positive power of $d/p$ is zero, while Theorem A has $\u03b4_0/a\u22648/r_p\u21920$. This refutes the workspace benchmark on its literal parameter range.\n\nFor the positive-degree consequence, set $d_p=floor(sqrt(r_p))$. Then $K_{d_p}log p=o(p)$, so Theorem A applies for all sufficiently large primes. Moreover,\n\n$$\na/(d_p/p)\u2265r_p/(4d_p)\u2192\u221e,\n$$\n\nwhereas $\u03b4_{d_p}/a\u22648/r_p\u21920$. Given any proposed constants $C,c>0$, large enough $p$ therefore satisfies both $a\u2265Cd_p/p$ and $\u03b4_{d_p}<ca$.\n\n**[P6, proved] Spectral repair at degree zero.** For each $z\u2208F_p$, let $X_z=\\{x:f(x)=z\\}$ and let $T_z=\\{L:P_L\u2261z\\}$. Write $u_z=|X_z|/p^2$ and $v_z=|T_z|/[p(p+1)]$. These are probability vectors. KTZ Lemma 2.1 gives\n\n$$\nPr[x\u2208X_z,L\u2208T_z]\u2264u_zv_z+sqrt(u_zv_z)/sqrt(p+1).\n$$\n\nSumming over $z$,\n\n$$\na\u2264\u03a3_z u_zv_z+(1/sqrt(p+1))\u03a3_z sqrt(u_zv_z)\n  \u2264max_z u_z+1/sqrt(p+1).\n$$\n\nThe last step uses Cauchy\u2013Schwarz exactly once: $\u03a3_z sqrt(u_zv_z)\u22641$. Since $max_z u_z=\u03b4_0$, Theorem B follows. There is no hidden Markov or union loss.\n\n**[P7, proved] Algebraic realization of the regular obstruction.** Fix $S\u2286F_p$ of size $k$ and set $f(x,y)=x^k$. Parameterize finite-slope lines by\n\n$$\nL_{m,b}(t)=(t,mt+b).\n$$\n\nDefine\n\n$$\nP_{m,b}(t)=t^k-\u220f_{s\u2208S}(t+m-s).\n$$\n\nThe two displayed summands are monic of degree $k$, so their leading terms cancel and $deg P_{m,b}\u2264k-1=d$. On a vertical line $V_c(t)=(c,t)$, set $P_{V_c}(t)=c^k+1$, which never equals $f(c,t)=c^k$.\n\nOn a finite-slope line, $P_{m,b}(t)=f(L_{m,b}(t))$ exactly when $t+m\u2208S$. Thus every finite-slope line has exactly $k$ accepted points. At a point $(x,y)$, exactly the $k$ slopes $m\u2208S-x$ are accepted, while the vertical line is never accepted. The accepted graph between all points and finite-slope lines is therefore exactly $k$-regular. Its local agreement under the required all-line sampling is\n\n$$\na=kp^2/[p^2(p+1)]=k/(p+1).\n$$\n\n**[P8, proved] Witness counting forces $p/\u03b5$ lines.** Let $C_R$ be the accepted incidences covered by another accepted line in $R$. Each selected finite-slope line contains $k$ accepted points; at each such point there are exactly $k-1$ other accepted lines. Hence the number of witness triples $(x,L,M)$ with $M\u2208R$, $L\u2260M$, and both incidences accepted is at most $|R|k(k-1)$. Multiple witnesses only overcount $C_R$, so\n\n$$\n|C_R|\u2264|R|k(k-1).\n$$\n\nCovering a $\u03b3$ fraction of the $kp^2$ accepted incidences requires $|C_R|\u2265\u03b3kp^2$. Therefore\n\n$$\n|R|\u2265\u03b3p^2/(k-1)\u2265\u03b3p/\u03b5_k,\n$$\n\nwhere the last inequality uses $k\u2264p$. Requiring this coverage on every line is stronger and gives the same bound. If selected-line edges were instead declared automatically covered, a modified count still yields $|R|=\u03a9(p/\u03b5_k)$.\n\n**[P9, proved] The obstruction table itself remains globally sound.** For every total-degree-at-most-$(k-1)$ polynomial $Q$ and each fixed $y$, the formal polynomial $X^k-Q(X,y)$ has degree exactly $k$, so it has at most $k$ roots in $F_p$. Thus $\u03b4_{k-1}\u2264k/p$. Equality is achieved by\n\n$$\nQ_S(X,Y)=X^k-\u220f_{s\u2208S}(X-s),\n$$\n\nwhose leading terms cancel and whose degree is at most $k-1$. Therefore $\u03b4_{k-1}=k/p=(1+1/p)\u03b5_k$. The example is not a soundness counterexample; it isolates the concentration architecture.\n\n**[P10, proved] The cubic bottleneck is reconstructed.** KTZ Lemma 3.2 gives $|R|=O(p/\u03b5)$. Weighted interpolation has $\u0398(D^3/d)$ available monomials and $O(|R|D)$ constraints, so it selects\n\n$$\nD=\u0398(sqrt(d|R|))=O(sqrt(dp/\u03b5)).\n$$\n\nExtending the line identity and surviving the second pruning require $D<k_1/2$ with $k_1=\u0398(\u03b5p)$. Hence\n\n$$\nsqrt(dp/\u03b5)=O(\u03b5p)\\quad iff\\quad \u03b5^3=\u03a9(d/p).\n$$\n\nTheorem C proves that the $p/\u03b5$ input to this calculation cannot be improved using only the accepted graph and the same witness requirement. It does not rule out a hybrid lemma exploiting the actual polynomial labels.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|\n| Modal occupancy | $p$ balls, $p$ colors | probability factor $1/2$ | load $r_p/2$ |\n| Deterministic extraction | load $r_p/2$ | conditioning factor $1/2$ | $a\u2265r_p/(4p)$ |\n| Global code union | $p^{K_d}$ candidates | $e^{K_d log p}$ | $\u03b4_d\u22642/p$ if $K_d log p\u2264\u03bbp/2$ |\n| Linear conversion | $a\u2265r_p/(4p)$ | ratio $8/r_p$ | $\u03b4_d=o(a)$ |\n| Exact exponent 1 | $d_p=sqrt(r_p)$ | $a/(d_p/p)\u2192\u221e$ | bare $Cd/p$ threshold refuted |\n| Degree-zero repair | local $a$ | additive $1/sqrt(p+1)$ by Cauchy\u2013Schwarz | $\u03b4_0\u2265a-1/sqrt(p+1)$ |\n| KTZ sparsification | minimum degree $\u0398(\u03b5p)$ | sampling probability $\u0398(1/(\u03b5p))$ | $|R|=O(p/\u03b5)$ |\n| New lower bound | regular accepted graph | witness capacity $k(k-1)$ per selected line | $|R|=\u03a9(p/\u03b5)$ |\n| KTZ interpolation | $|R|=\u0398(p/\u03b5)$ | $D^3/d$ versus $|R|D$ | $D=\u0398(sqrt(dp/\u03b5))$ |\n| Root propagation | degree $D$ | require $D=O(\u03b5p)$ | $\u03b5^3=\u03a9(d/p)$ |\n\nAll displayed exponent manipulations are included. No logarithm has been suppressed in a claimed power threshold.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Random modal-color table \u2014 successful.** This proves Theorem A and refutes the literal $d=0$ benchmark and a bare exact-linear threshold in a growing positive-degree regime.\n2. **Regular algebraic incidence table \u2014 successful as an architectural obstruction.** Theorem C matches the KTZ $p/\u03b5$ selector size but has global agreement $(1+1/p)\u03b5$, so it does not refute soundness.\n3. **Concentrated good directions \u2014 not worst case.** Taking $f=0$, setting $P_L=0$ on $s$ directions and $P_L=1$ elsewhere gives local agreement $s/(p+1)$. Its accepted graph can be covered at scale $\u0398(p)$ rather than $\u0398(p/\u03b5)$; concentrated directions therefore do not explain the cubic bottleneck.\n4. **Small primes.** Exhaustive enumeration gives ratio $4/3$ at $p=2,d=0$ and $7/4$ at $p=3,d=0$. These do not prove divergence, but they reveal no exceptional collapse.\n5. **Near-maximal degree.** Theorem C permits $k=p,d=p-1$. Then $\u220f_{s\u2208F_p}(t-s)=t^p-t$ and all degree claims remain valid.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The probabilistic counterexample uses only iid values in $F_p$ and constant line polynomials. It has no separability assumption.\n- Theorem C uses distinct linear roots. At $k=p$, $t^p-t$ is squarefree because its derivative is $-1$. There is no hidden division by $k$, $d$, or a derivative.\n- No discriminant, resultant, irreducibility claim, Hasse derivative, or interpolation multiplicity appears in the new proofs.\n- KTZ's derivative and Newton-lifting machinery is not used to prove any new claim. Its division-by-$d$ monomial bound is precisely why its printed proof does not cover $d=0$.\n- The only Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss is the explicit $1/sqrt(p+1)$ term in [P6]. The only global union loss is $p^{K_d}$. No Markov inequality is used. Poisson and Chernoff losses are displayed in [P2]\u2013[P4].\n- The line model is the full affine set, including vertical lines. Total degree is never replaced by individual degree. All auxiliary constructions obey $d<p$.\n- Finite computations were used solely for falsification; the asymptotic theorem is probabilistic but rigorous.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThis note proves no exponent greater than $1/3$ for $1\u2264d<p$. The occupancy construction lies below every fixed-$\u03b7$ threshold $(d/p)^{1-\u03b7}$ along the displayed growing-degree sequence, so the principal near-linear target remains open.\n\nThe degree-zero repair has a gap: the counterexample forces a floor of at least order $log p/(p log log p)$, while the spectral argument only proves linear recovery above order $p^{-1/2}$. The exact floor is undetermined.\n\nThe sparsifier lower bound applies to the KTZ witness definition, or any method based only on the accepted incidence graph. It does not preclude using polynomial coefficients, higher-order algebraic coincidences, or a simultaneous algebraic-concentration argument. Indeed, that is now the necessary next direction.\n\nFinally, the cited HKSS source is arXiv v1 and contains unresolved internal exponent bookkeeping. Their combination is `\u03b5\u00b3 = \u03a9(d/p)`.\n\nRetaining the fraction \u03c3 of lines supporting an accepted carrier of edge mass \u03b4 gives the sharper proved relation `\u03b4\u00b3 = \u03a9(d\u03c3/p)`. In particular, \u03c3=O(\u03b4) gives a conditional exponent `1/2`, but not an unconditional benchmark improvement. In the prime regime, I also prove that the primitive squarefree interpolant satisfies `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`, so KTZ's generic directional derivative can be replaced by the vertical derivative.\n\nFinally, I give a legal obstruction at ambient degree `d=101`: modal constant line labels can attain local agreement `\u0398(log p/(p log log p))` while every total-degree-at-most-101 polynomial has agreement below `2/p`. Thus a uniform exact threshold `C d/p` with global agreement `\u03a9(\u03b5)` is false. This obstruction remains below every fixed-\u03b7 trigger `(d/p)^(1\u2212\u03b7)`.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix a prime `p` and an integer `101\u2264d<p`; the dimension is exactly two. Let `L` range uniformly over the `p(p+1)` affine lines of `F_p\u00b2`, and then let `x` range uniformly over the `p` points of `L`. This is uniform sampling from the `p\u00b2(p+1)` incidences and is equivalent to first choosing `x` uniformly and then an incident line uniformly.\n\nThe point table is an arbitrary function `f:F_p\u00b2\u2192F_p`. Each line has a univariate polynomial label `P_L` of degree at most `d`. All global degrees below are total degrees. Define\n\n`\u03b5 = Pr_{L,x\u2208L}[P_L(x)=f(x)]`\n\nand\n\n`Agr_d(f) = max_{Q: total-degree(Q)\u2264d} Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]`.\n\nAn accepted carrier is any set `E*` of accepted incidences. Write\n\n`\u03b4 = |E*|/[p\u00b2(p+1)]`,  `T = projection of E* to lines`,  `\u03c3 = |T|/[p(p+1)]`.\n\nNecessarily `0<\u03b4\u2264\u03c3\u22641`. Taking all accepted incidences gives `\u03b4=\u03b5`; a carrier with `\u03b4\u2265\u03b5/2` retains a constant fraction of the test acceptance.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe primary benchmark is [Kominers\u2013Thaler\u2013Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, Revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/). Its Theorem 1.1, specialized to the present regime, states that absolute constants `C,c>0` give global agreement at least `c\u03b5` when `\u03b5\u2265C(d/p)^(1/3)`. The theorem statement hides the constants. The bivariate proof in Sections 3\u20136 explicitly closes with recovery `\u03b5/8000`.\n\nThe source chooses `k0=floor(\u03b5p/100)`, `k1=floor(\u03b5p/1000)`, a selected line set of size `O(p/\u03b5)`, and\n\n`D = 16(floor(sqrt(d|R|))+1)`.\n\nRevision 1 uses a squarefree primitive polynomial, a generic directional derivative, and a resultant; it does not use a discriminant in the bivariate proof. The constant `10^15` below is my conservative reconstruction for a support-sensitive variant, not a constant quoted from Theorem 1.1. The older cached base report and Revision 1 must not be conflated.\n\nThe Newton step is consistent with [Harsha\u2013Kumar\u2013Saptharishi\u2013Sudan, arXiv:2311.12752v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12752), especially Lemma 2.10, but the needed lifting argument is reproduced below. No Arora\u2013Sudan theorem is used as a black box.\n\nThe active durable corpus was also audited. All eight active leaderboard files were empty, and there were no completed submissions or verifier-audit files to inherit. The [data manifest](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/DATA_MANIFEST.json) is a pre-launch snapshot relative to the live campaign state, so it was treated as provenance rather than mathematical evidence. Every directory named `superseded` was excluded.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A \u2014 support-sensitive KTZ closure.** Let `p` be prime, `101\u2264d<p`, and let an accepted carrier have parameters `(\u03b4,\u03c3)`. Put `K=10^15`. If\n\n`\u03b4\u00b3 \u2265 K d\u03c3/p`,\n\nthen there is a polynomial `Q\u2208F_p[X,Y]` of total degree at most `d` with\n\n`Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)] \u2265 \u03b4/8000`.\n\nThus, if `\u03b4\u2265\u03b5/2`, the conclusion is at least `\u03b5/16000`. With all accepted edges and \u03c3\u22641, the sufficient threshold is `\u03b5\u226510^5(d/p)^(1/3)`. Under the additional structural condition `\u03c3\u2264A\u03b4`, it becomes the conditional square-root threshold `\u03b4\u2265sqrt(10^15 A d/p)`.\n\n**Lemma B \u2014 prime vertical derivative.** If `B\u2208F_p[X,Y,Z]` is squarefree, primitive as a polynomial in `Z`, and has total degree below `p`, then `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`.\n\n**Theorem C \u2014 modal obstruction at the legal lower boundary.** Let `d=101`, `N=(d+1)(d+2)/2=5253`, and\n\n`r=floor(log p/(4 log log p))`.\n\nFor every sufficiently large prime, explicitly every prime `p\u2265max{\u2308e^32\u2309,100N\u00b2}`, there are a point table and constant line labels, hence labels of degree at most 101, such that\n\n`r/(130p) \u2264 \u03b5 \u2264 50r/p`,  while  `Agr_101(f)<2/p`.\n\nConsequently, for every fixed `C,c>0`, arbitrarily large primes admit `\u03b5\u2265C\u00b7101/p` but `Agr_101(f)<c\u03b5`.\n\n**Proposition D \u2014 near-p information baseline.** For every `101\u2264d<p` and every point table,\n\n`Agr_d(f) \u2265 (d+1)(d+2)/(2p\u00b2)`.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1] (proved) Carrier pruning.** Set `k0=floor(\u03b4p/100)`. Iteratively delete point vertices and line vertices whose current carrier degree is below `k0`. Point deletions remove at most `p\u00b2k0` edges and line deletions at most `p(p+1)k0` edges. In normalized incidence measure the loss is at most\n\n`k0/(p+1)+k0/p < \u03b4/50`.\n\nKeep the weaker bound that the remaining graph `G0` has edge mass at least `\u03b4/4`. It has minimum degree `k0`; its line set `L0` has normalized measure \u03bb satisfying `\u03b4/4\u2264\u03bb\u2264\u03c3`.\n\n**[P2] (proved) Support-sensitive selector.** Select each line of `L0` independently with probability `\u03b8=8/k0`. The hypothesis and `\u03c3\u2265\u03b4` imply\n\n`\u03b4\u00b2\u226510^15 d/p`,  `\u03b4p\u2265sqrt(10^15dp)>3\u00b710^9`,\n\nso `k0\u2265\u03b4p/200`. For a fixed `L\u2208L0`, coverage indicators at distinct neighbors of `L` depend on disjoint sets of other lines. Each has success probability above `3/4`; Hoeffding therefore bounds failure to cover half the neighbors by `exp(\u2212k0/8)`. Since `k0\u22658 log(4p(p+1))`, a union bound over all affine lines costs less than `1/4`.\n\nIf `r=|R|`, then `E[r]=\u03b8|L0|\u2265200(p+1)` and `Var(r)\u2264E[r]`. Chebyshev puts `r` between half and twice its mean with failure below `1/4`. Some deterministic selection consequently satisfies both coverage and\n\n`100(p+1)\u2264r\u226416|L0|/k0\u22646400\u03c3p/\u03b4`.\n\nThese are the only Hoeffding, selector union, and Chebyshev losses.\n\n**[P3] (proved) Weighted interpolation.** Give `X,Y,Z` weights `1,1,d` and set\n\n`D=16(floor(sqrt(dr))+1)`.\n\nThen `D\u00b2>256dr` and KTZ's monomial count gives `dim(V_D)\u2265D\u00b3/(64d)>r(D+1)`. Each formal identity `A(L(t),P_L(t))=0` imposes at most `D+1` coefficient equations, so a nonzero interpolant exists. Moreover,\n\n`D\u22641280 sqrt(d\u03c3p/\u03b4)+16\u22641280\u03b4p/sqrt(10^15)+16<\u03b4p/10000`.\n\nThus `D<p`, `D<k0/2`, and, for `k1=floor(\u03b4p/1000)`, `D<k1/2`. Also `r>D`. A nonzero `Z`-independent polynomial of degree at most `D` cannot vanish identically on more than `D` affine lines, so `A_Z\u22600`. Choosing minimum weighted degree removes repeated factors and makes `A` squarefree.\n\n**[P4] (proved) Identity extension and formal content removal.** Every `L\u2208L0` has more than `k0/2>D` distinct accepted points that also lie on selected accepted lines. At each such point the two line labels equal the same value `f(x)`. Hence the degree-at-most-`D` polynomial `A(L(t),P_L(t))` has more than `D` distinct roots and is identically zero.\n\nWrite `A=H(X,Y)B(X,Y,Z)`, where `H` is the gcd of the coefficients in `Z`. At most `deg(H)\u2264D` base lines satisfy `H|_L=0` identically. On every other retained line, `H(L(t))B(L(t),P_L(t))=0` in the integral domain `F_p[t]`; hence `B(L(t),P_L(t))=0`. This is formal polynomial division, not division by values of `H`. No root multiplicities are counted.\n\n**[P5] (proved) Prime vertical-derivative lemma.** Factor the squarefree primitive polynomial as `B=c\u220fP_i` into distinct irreducibles over `F_p`. Primitivity implies that every `P_i` genuinely depends on `Z`. Since `deg_Z(P_i)<p`, its derivative `(P_i)_Z` is nonzero, and its smaller degree implies `P_i` does not divide `(P_i)_Z`. Modulo `P_i`,\n\n`B_Z = (P_i)_Z \u220f_{j\u2260i}P_j \u22600`.\n\nThus no irreducible factor of `B` divides `B_Z`, proving `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`. No irreducibility over the algebraic closure is required. This replaces, in the prime-field regime only, KTZ's generic directional derivative.\n\n**[P6] (proved) Degenerate-root deletion.** Apply KTZ's resultant line bound to the coprime pair `(B,B_Z)`. Delete the at most `D` content lines, at most `D(D\u22121)` lines on which the two graph identities degenerate together, and at most `D` zeros of `B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))` on every other line. Their total normalized edge mass is bounded by\n\n`D/[p(p+1)] + D(D\u22121)/[p(p+1)] + D/p < \u03b4/16`.\n\nPruning both sides at degree `k1=floor(\u03b4p/1000)` costs at most\n\n`k1/(p+1)+k1/p<\u03b4/500`.\n\nThe surviving graph `G1` has edge mass at least `\u03b4/8`, minimum degree `k1`, and `B_Z(x,f(x))\u22600` at every surviving point. No discriminant or Markov inequality appears.\n\n**[P7] (proved) Hensel lifting and propagation.** At a surviving point translate the base coordinates to `(0,0)` and put `\u03b1=f(0,0)`. In `F_p[[X,Y]]`, construct a root `\u03a6=\u03b1+\u03a6_1+\u03a6_2+\u2026` recursively by homogeneous degree. At stage `j`, the degree-`j` residual is canceled uniquely by division by the scalar `B_Z(0,0,\u03b1)`. Thus no factorial is inverted.\n\nEvery incident line polynomial is the same unique root after restriction to that line. There are more than `D` incident directions. Therefore every homogeneous part `\u03a6_j` with `d<j\u2264D` vanishes on more than `D\u2265j` projective directions and is zero. Let `Q` be the truncation through degree `d`. The polynomial `B(X,Y,Q)` has degree at most `D` and all terms through degree `D` vanish, so it is identically zero. Simple-root uniqueness propagates the same `Q` across every edge of the connected component, and `Q=f` at all of its point vertices.\n\n**[P8] (proved) Component mixing and recovery.** For a component let `a,b,e` denote its normalized point, line, and edge measures. Put `\u03ba=k1/p` and `u=1/sqrt(p+1)`. Minimum degree and point-line mixing give\n\n`e\u2265\u03baa/2`,  `e\u2265\u03bab`,  and  `e\u2264ab+u sqrt(ab)`.\n\nThe theorem hypothesis gives `u<\u03b4/8000\u2264\u03ba/4`. If `a<\u03ba/4`, the last two inequalities imply `9b\u2264a`, which contradicts the first inequality. If `b<\u03ba/4`, they imply `a\u2264b`, which contradicts `e\u2265\u03bab`. Hence `a,b\u2265\u03ba/4\u2265\u03b4/8000`. The polynomial from [P7] therefore has global agreement at least `\u03b4/8000`. This is the sole incidence Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss.\n\n**[P9] (proved) Exact cubic reconstruction.** The dominant scales are\n\n`r=O(\u03c3p/\u03b4)`,  `D=O(sqrt(d\u03c3p/\u03b4))`,  `D=O(\u03b4p)`.\n\nThe first two give the interpolation degree; the last is independently demanded by identity extension, the `D/p` bad-incidence term, and lifting. Squaring the final comparison yields exactly `\u03b4\u00b3=\u03a9(d\u03c3/p)`. The resultant term `D\u00b2/p\u00b2` alone needs only `\u03b4\u00b2=\u03a9(d\u03c3/p)`, and mixing needs only `\u03b4=\u03a9(p^\u22121/2)`; both are weaker here. For \u03c3=1 this is the KTZ cubic exponent.\n\n**[P10] (conditional) Concentrated-carrier exponent.** If additionally `\u03c3\u2264A\u03b4`, [P9] becomes `\u03b4\u00b2=\u03a9(Ad/p)`, giving exponent `1/2`. Since every carrier has `\u03c3\u2265\u03b4`, this support-sensitive interpolation balance cannot exceed exponent `1/2`. This is not an unconditional improvement of the benchmark.\n\n**[P11] (proved) Modal occupancy lower bound.** For Theorem C choose all `p\u00b2` point values independently and uniformly. On a fixed line let `N_a` be the occupancy of value `a`, `M=max_a N_a`, and `Y=\u03a3_a 1[N_a=r]`. For one value,\n\n`Pr[N_a=r] = binom(p,r)p^(\u2212r)(1\u22121/p)^(p\u2212r) \u2265 1/(8r!)`.\n\nHere `r\u00b2\u2264p`, `(1\u22121/p)^p\u22651/4`, and `r!\u2264r^r\u2264p^(1/4)`. Thus `\u03bc=E[Y]\u2265p^(3/4)/8\u22651`. For distinct values, the joint probability of both occupancies equaling `r` is at most `1/(r!)\u00b2`, at most 64 times the product of the lower bounds. Hence `E[Y\u00b2]\u2264\u03bc+64\u03bc\u00b2\u226465\u03bc\u00b2`. Cauchy\u2013Schwarz, equivalently the zero-threshold Paley\u2013Zygmund argument, gives `Pr[Y>0]\u22651/65`, so `E[M]\u2265r/65`.\n\nGive each line a modal constant label. By linearity of expectation across lines\u2014no line independence is asserted\u2014the local agreement `A` satisfies `E[A]\u2265r/(65p)`.\n\n**[P12] (proved) Modal upper concentration.** A factorial-moment union bound gives\n\n`Pr[M\u2265s]\u2264p/s!\u2264p(e/s)^s`.\n\nFor `s0=ceil(4 log p/log log p)`, the tail sums to less than one and `E[M]\u2264s0+1\u226425r`; hence `E[A]\u226425r/p`. Changing one point value changes the modal count on only its `p+1` incident lines and changes `A` by at most `1/p\u00b2`. McDiarmid therefore gives\n\n`Pr[A>50r/p]\u2264exp(\u22121250r\u00b2)\u2264r/(520p)`.\n\nNo Markov inequality is used.\n\n**[P13] (proved) Global union bound and deterministic instance.** There are `p^N` formal total-degree-at-most-101 polynomials, with `N=5253`. For fixed `Q`, its agreement count with random `f` is `Bin(p\u00b2,1/p)`, of mean `p`. Chernoff gives\n\n`Pr[agreements(Q,f)\u22652p]\u2264(e/4)^p`.\n\nUnion over all `p^N` polynomials gives `p^N(e/4)^p\u2264exp(\u2212p/4)\u2264r/(520p)` under the stated lower bound on `p`. Let `G` be the event that all global agreements are below `2/p`, and `H={A\u226450r/p}`. Since `0\u2264A\u22641`,\n\n`E[A\u00b71_{G\u2229H}] \u2265 r/(65p)\u2212r/(520p)\u2212r/(520p) > r/(130p)`.\n\nSome deterministic table in `G\u2229H` therefore has all three bounds in Theorem C.\n\n**[P14] (refuted) Uniform exact-linear soundness.** Suppose constants `C,c>0` made `\u03b5\u2265Cd/p` imply `Agr_d(f)\u2265c\u03b5` uniformly. Fix the legal ambient cap `d=101` and choose a sufficiently large prime with `r\u2265max{130\u00b7101C,260/c}`. Theorem C then has `\u03b5\u2265C\u00b7101/p` but `Agr_101(f)<2/p<c\u03b5`, a contradiction. Thus the exact-linear statement is false. On the other hand, for each fixed `\u03b7>0`,\n\n`\u03b5/(101/p)^(1\u2212\u03b7) \u2264 50r/[101^(1\u2212\u03b7)p^\u03b7] \u2192 0`,\n\nso this construction does not refute a fixed-\u03b7 target.\n\n**[P15] (proved) Near-p information set.** Choose distinct `a_0,\u2026,a_d` and `b_0,\u2026,b_d` and the triangular set `S={(a_i,b_j):i+j\u2264d}`. The Newton products `\u220f_{h<i}(X\u2212a_h)\u220f_{k<j}(Y\u2212b_k)` with `i+j\u2264d` form a triangular evaluation basis on `S`. Hence arbitrary prescribed values on all `|S|=(d+1)(d+2)/2` points extend to a total-degree-at-most-`d` polynomial. Applying this to `f|_S` proves Proposition D. In particular, the lower bound is `(p+1)/(2p)` at `d=p\u22121` and `5253/10609` at `d=101,p=103`.\n\n**[P16] (proved) Diffuse support need not concentrate.** Fix the legal ambient `d\u2265101`, take `f=0`, and on every line choose a degree-`d` label with `d` distinct prescribed parameter roots. Then `\u03b5=d/p` and every line supports acceptance, so `\u03c3=1`; nevertheless `Q=0` agrees globally everywhere. Thus local density does not imply `\u03c3=O(\u03b5)`, although this example is harmless for soundness.\n\n**[P17] (refuted as an obstruction) Concentrated good directions.** Let `f` be a product of `d+1` distinct homogeneous linear forms. In each of the corresponding `d+1` projective directions, every affine-line restriction loses its degree-`d+1` leading term and is a legal degree-`d` label. This gives local mass about `(d+1)/(p+1)`. But `Q=0` agrees on the union of the same `d+1` lines through the origin, a \u0398(d/p) fraction. The attempted counterexample already contains the required global polynomial.\n\n**[P18] (refuted safety of omitting simplicity) Branch collision.** For odd `p` and legal ambient cap `d\u2265101`, `B=Z\u00b2\u2212X\u00b2` is squarefree but its two legal branches `Q=X` and `Q=\u2212X` meet at the origin, where `B_Z=0`. Agreement at that incidence cannot select a branch. Vertical-simple-root deletion is therefore logically necessary.\n\n**[P19] (refuted as an active obstruction) Inseparability.** A polynomial with vanishing `Z`-derivative must use positive `Z`-exponents divisible by `p`. Since the interpolant has weighted degree `D<p`, no such exponent occurs. Examples such as `Z^p\u2212G` lie outside the interpolation space and do not obstruct the prime-field proof.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Scale or loss | Consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| Carrier pruning | `<\u03b4/50`, retained as `\u03b4/4` | Constant only |\n| Selector probability | Hoeffding `e^(\u2212k0/8)`, union over `p(p+1)` | No \u03b4-power loss |\n| Selector size | Chebyshev; `r\u22646400\u03c3p/\u03b4` | One factor `\u03c3/\u03b4` |\n| Interpolation | `dim(V_D)\u2248D\u00b3/d` versus `rD` constraints | `D\u2248sqrt(dr)` |\n| Root budget | `D\u2264\u0398(\u03b4p)` | `\u03b4\u00b3=\u03a9(d\u03c3/p)` |\n| Content/resultant deletion | `D/p + D\u00b2/p\u00b2` | Cubic plus a weaker quadratic gate |\n| Second pruning | `<\u03b4/500` | Constant only |\n| Mixing | One Cauchy\u2013Schwarz error `p^\u22121/2` | Weaker than cubic for `d\u2265101` |\n| Recovery | Component point density `\u03b4/8000` | Linear global recovery |\n| Diffuse carrier | `\u03c3=1` | Exponent `1/3` |\n| Concentrated carrier | `\u03c3\u2264A\u03b4` | Conditional exponent `1/2` |\n| Modal occupancy | `r\u2248log p/(4 log log p)` | Local `\u0398(r/p)` |\n| Polynomial union | `p^5253(e/4)^p` | Global `<2/p` |\n| Exact-linear claim | Ratio at most `260/r` | Tends to zero; exponent 1 with constant threshold is false |\n\nThere is no hidden Markov loss. The only probabilistic inequalities are the selector's Hoeffding, union, and Chebyshev bounds; the modal occupancy second moment, factorial union, and McDiarmid bound; and the global Chernoff union. The sole incidence Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss is the `p^\u22121/2` mixing error.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\nThe successful adversarial table is Theorem C: it is diffuse across lines and exploits the maximum occupancy among `p` symbols, not low characteristic or a small exceptional direction set. It proves that the campaign's possible sharp threshold cannot literally be a constant multiple of `d/p` with linear recovery.\n\nThe all-lines prescribed-root table [P16] shows why line-support concentration cannot be assumed. The homogeneous-direction construction [P17] fails because its zero set already supplies a global polynomial. The branch collision [P18] validates the simple-root deletion. The inseparable attempt [P19] is excluded by `D<p`. Proposition D handles `d` near `p`; it is a positive agreement baseline, not an obstruction.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The field is exactly the prime field `F_p`; no extension-field descent is used.\n- The ambient degree always satisfies `101\u2264d<p`. Constant or linear objects appearing inside examples are legal labels or branches under that ambient cap; no test with parameter `d\u2264100` is analyzed.\n- Because `D<p`, the characteristic-pruned weighted monomial set equals the full weighted ball: every positive `Z`-exponent is strictly below `p`.\n- Lemma B rules out inseparable vertical factors after content removal. Absolute irreducibility is unnecessary.\n- KTZ's source proof uses a generic directional derivative. The replacement by `B_Z` is a new prime-field simplification and causes no exponent gain.\n- No discriminant is used. The resultant is invoked only for the proved coprime pair `(B,B_Z)`.\n- Division by `H` occurs only as an integral-domain inference on non-content lines. Hensel lifting divides only by a nonzero scalar `B_Z(x,f(x))`.\n- All interpolation constraints are coefficient identities, and every later root count uses distinct points or directions rather than multiplicity.\n- When `d` is near `p`, Theorem A's premise is vacuous because `\u03c3\u2265\u03b4` would force `p\u226510^15d`; Proposition D supplies the appropriate direct check.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe general KTZ benchmark is not improved: the exponent `1/2` conclusion requires the additional hypothesis `\u03c3=O(\u03b4)`, and diffuse carriers can have `\u03c3=1`. The constant `10^15` is deliberately conservative and is not claimed optimal.\n\nThe modal obstruction refutes a uniform constant-times-`d/p` trigger but not any fixed exponent `1\u2212\u03b7`. It instead shows that an exponent-1 formulation must include a subpolynomial occupancy allowance, at least on the order of `log p/log log p` when `d=101`.\n\nThe current selector has an upper bound `O(\u03c3p/\u03b4)`, whereas covering more than `k0/2` points on one line requires at least `\u03a9(\u03b4p)` distinct witness lines. Closing this gap demands a new combinatorial or algebraic idea. No computation, higher-dimensional lifting, extension field, or individual-degree substitution is used here.",
