Their combination is `ε³ = Ω(d/p)`.\n\nRetaining the fraction σ of lines supporting an accepted carrier of edge mass δ gives the sharper proved relation `δ³ = Ω(dσ/p)`. In particular, σ=O(δ) gives a conditional exponent `1/2`, but not an unconditional benchmark improvement. In the prime regime, I also prove that the primitive squarefree interpolant satisfies `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`, so KTZ's generic directional derivative can be replaced by the vertical derivative.\n\nFinally, I give a legal obstruction at ambient degree `d=101`: modal constant line labels can attain local agreement `Θ(log p/(p log log p))` while every total-degree-at-most-101 polynomial has agreement below `2/p`. Thus a uniform exact threshold `C d/p` with global agreement `Ω(ε)` is false. This obstruction remains below every fixed-η trigger `(d/p)^(1−η)`.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nFix a prime `p` and an integer `101≤d<p`; the dimension is exactly two. Let `L` range uniformly over the `p(p+1)` affine lines of `F_p²`, and then let `x` range uniformly over the `p` points of `L`. This is uniform sampling from the `p²(p+1)` incidences and is equivalent to first choosing `x` uniformly and then an incident line uniformly.\n\nThe point table is an arbitrary function `f:F_p²→F_p`. Each line has a univariate polynomial label `P_L` of degree at most `d`. All global degrees below are total degrees. Define\n\n`ε = Pr_{L,x∈L}[P_L(x)=f(x)]`\n\nand\n\n`Agr_d(f) = max_{Q: total-degree(Q)≤d} Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]`.\n\nAn accepted carrier is any set `E*` of accepted incidences. Write\n\n`δ = |E*|/[p²(p+1)]`,  `T = projection of E* to lines`,  `σ = |T|/[p(p+1)]`.\n\nNecessarily `0<δ≤σ≤1`. Taking all accepted incidences gives `δ=ε`; a carrier with `δ≥ε/2` retains a constant fraction of the test acceptance.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe primary benchmark is [Kominers–Thaler–Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, Revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/). Its Theorem 1.1, specialized to the present regime, states that absolute constants `C,c>0` give global agreement at least `cε` when `ε≥C(d/p)^(1/3)`. The theorem statement hides the constants. The bivariate proof in Sections 3–6 explicitly closes with recovery `ε/8000`.\n\nThe source chooses `k0=floor(εp/100)`, `k1=floor(εp/1000)`, a selected line set of size `O(p/ε)`, and\n\n`D = 16(floor(sqrt(d|R|))+1)`.\n\nRevision 1 uses a squarefree primitive polynomial, a generic directional derivative, and a resultant; it does not use a discriminant in the bivariate proof. The constant `10^15` below is my conservative reconstruction for a support-sensitive variant, not a constant quoted from Theorem 1.1. The older cached base report and Revision 1 must not be conflated.\n\nThe Newton step is consistent with [Harsha–Kumar–Saptharishi–Sudan, arXiv:2311.12752v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12752), especially Lemma 2.10, but the needed lifting argument is reproduced below. No Arora–Sudan theorem is used as a black box.\n\nThe active durable corpus was also audited. All eight active leaderboard files were empty, and there were no completed submissions or verifier-audit files to inherit. The [data manifest](/Users/kaizheng/Documents/ChatGPT/Line-vs-Point/research_state/DATA_MANIFEST.json) is a pre-launch snapshot relative to the live campaign state, so it was treated as provenance rather than mathematical evidence. Every directory named `superseded` was excluded.\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem A — support-sensitive KTZ closure.** Let `p` be prime, `101≤d<p`, and let an accepted carrier have parameters `(δ,σ)`. Put `K=10^15`. If\n\n`δ³ ≥ K dσ/p`,\n\nthen there is a polynomial `Q∈F_p[X,Y]` of total degree at most `d` with\n\n`Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)] ≥ δ/8000`.\n\nThus, if `δ≥ε/2`, the conclusion is at least `ε/16000`. With all accepted edges and σ≤1, the sufficient threshold is `ε≥10^5(d/p)^(1/3)`. Under the additional structural condition `σ≤Aδ`, it becomes the conditional square-root threshold `δ≥sqrt(10^15 A d/p)`.\n\n**Lemma B — prime vertical derivative.** If `B∈F_p[X,Y,Z]` is squarefree, primitive as a polynomial in `Z`, and has total degree below `p`, then `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`.\n\n**Theorem C — modal obstruction at the legal lower boundary.** Let `d=101`, `N=(d+1)(d+2)/2=5253`, and\n\n`r=floor(log p/(4 log log p))`.\n\nFor every sufficiently large prime, explicitly every prime `p≥max{⌈e^32⌉,100N²}`, there are a point table and constant line labels, hence labels of degree at most 101, such that\n\n`r/(130p) ≤ ε ≤ 50r/p`,  while  `Agr_101(f)<2/p`.\n\nConsequently, for every fixed `C,c>0`, arbitrarily large primes admit `ε≥C·101/p` but `Agr_101(f)<cε`.\n\n**Proposition D — near-p information baseline.** For every `101≤d<p` and every point table,\n\n`Agr_d(f) ≥ (d+1)(d+2)/(2p²)`.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1] (proved) Carrier pruning.** Set `k0=floor(δp/100)`. Iteratively delete point vertices and line vertices whose current carrier degree is below `k0`. Point deletions remove at most `p²k0` edges and line deletions at most `p(p+1)k0` edges. In normalized incidence measure the loss is at most\n\n`k0/(p+1)+k0/p < δ/50`.\n\nKeep the weaker bound that the remaining graph `G0` has edge mass at least `δ/4`. It has minimum degree `k0`; its line set `L0` has normalized measure λ satisfying `δ/4≤λ≤σ`.\n\n**[P2] (proved) Support-sensitive selector.** Select each line of `L0` independently with probability `θ=8/k0`. The hypothesis and `σ≥δ` imply\n\n`δ²≥10^15 d/p`,  `δp≥sqrt(10^15dp)>3·10^9`,\n\nso `k0≥δp/200`. For a fixed `L∈L0`, coverage indicators at distinct neighbors of `L` depend on disjoint sets of other lines. Each has success probability above `3/4`; Hoeffding therefore bounds failure to cover half the neighbors by `exp(−k0/8)`. Since `k0≥8 log(4p(p+1))`, a union bound over all affine lines costs less than `1/4`.\n\nIf `r=|R|`, then `E[r]=θ|L0|≥200(p+1)` and `Var(r)≤E[r]`. Chebyshev puts `r` between half and twice its mean with failure below `1/4`. Some deterministic selection consequently satisfies both coverage and\n\n`100(p+1)≤r≤16|L0|/k0≤6400σp/δ`.\n\nThese are the only Hoeffding, selector union, and Chebyshev losses.\n\n**[P3] (proved) Weighted interpolation.** Give `X,Y,Z` weights `1,1,d` and set\n\n`D=16(floor(sqrt(dr))+1)`.\n\nThen `D²>256dr` and KTZ's monomial count gives `dim(V_D)≥D³/(64d)>r(D+1)`. Each formal identity `A(L(t),P_L(t))=0` imposes at most `D+1` coefficient equations, so a nonzero interpolant exists. Moreover,\n\n`D≤1280 sqrt(dσp/δ)+16≤1280δp/sqrt(10^15)+16<δp/10000`.\n\nThus `D<p`, `D<k0/2`, and, for `k1=floor(δp/1000)`, `D<k1/2`. Also `r>D`. A nonzero `Z`-independent polynomial of degree at most `D` cannot vanish identically on more than `D` affine lines, so `A_Z≠0`. Choosing minimum weighted degree removes repeated factors and makes `A` squarefree.\n\n**[P4] (proved) Identity extension and formal content removal.** Every `L∈L0` has more than `k0/2>D` distinct accepted points that also lie on selected accepted lines. At each such point the two line labels equal the same value `f(x)`. Hence the degree-at-most-`D` polynomial `A(L(t),P_L(t))` has more than `D` distinct roots and is identically zero.\n\nWrite `A=H(X,Y)B(X,Y,Z)`, where `H` is the gcd of the coefficients in `Z`. At most `deg(H)≤D` base lines satisfy `H|_L=0` identically. On every other retained line, `H(L(t))B(L(t),P_L(t))=0` in the integral domain `F_p[t]`; hence `B(L(t),P_L(t))=0`. This is formal polynomial division, not division by values of `H`. No root multiplicities are counted.\n\n**[P5] (proved) Prime vertical-derivative lemma.** Factor the squarefree primitive polynomial as `B=c∏P_i` into distinct irreducibles over `F_p`. Primitivity implies that every `P_i` genuinely depends on `Z`. Since `deg_Z(P_i)<p`, its derivative `(P_i)_Z` is nonzero, and its smaller degree implies `P_i` does not divide `(P_i)_Z`. Modulo `P_i`,\n\n`B_Z = (P_i)_Z ∏_{j≠i}P_j ≠0`.\n\nThus no irreducible factor of `B` divides `B_Z`, proving `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`. No irreducibility over the algebraic closure is required. This replaces, in the prime-field regime only, KTZ's generic directional derivative.\n\n**[P6] (proved) Degenerate-root deletion.** Apply KTZ's resultant line bound to the coprime pair `(B,B_Z)`. Delete the at most `D` content lines, at most `D(D−1)` lines on which the two graph identities degenerate together, and at most `D` zeros of `B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))` on every other line. Their total normalized edge mass is bounded by\n\n`D/[p(p+1)] + D(D−1)/[p(p+1)] + D/p < δ/16`.\n\nPruning both sides at degree `k1=floor(δp/1000)` costs at most\n\n`k1/(p+1)+k1/p<δ/500`.\n\nThe surviving graph `G1` has edge mass at least `δ/8`, minimum degree `k1`, and `B_Z(x,f(x))≠0` at every surviving point. No discriminant or Markov inequality appears.\n\n**[P7] (proved) Hensel lifting and propagation.** At a surviving point translate the base coordinates to `(0,0)` and put `α=f(0,0)`. In `F_p[[X,Y]]`, construct a root `Φ=α+Φ_1+Φ_2+…` recursively by homogeneous degree. At stage `j`, the degree-`j` residual is canceled uniquely by division by the scalar `B_Z(0,0,α)`. Thus no factorial is inverted.\n\nEvery incident line polynomial is the same unique root after restriction to that line. There are more than `D` incident directions. Therefore every homogeneous part `Φ_j` with `d<j≤D` vanishes on more than `D≥j` projective directions and is zero. Let `Q` be the truncation through degree `d`. The polynomial `B(X,Y,Q)` has degree at most `D` and all terms through degree `D` vanish, so it is identically zero. Simple-root uniqueness propagates the same `Q` across every edge of the connected component, and `Q=f` at all of its point vertices.\n\n**[P8] (proved) Component mixing and recovery.** For a component let `a,b,e` denote its normalized point, line, and edge measures. Put `κ=k1/p` and `u=1/sqrt(p+1)`. Minimum degree and point-line mixing give\n\n`e≥κa/2`,  `e≥κb`,  and  `e≤ab+u sqrt(ab)`.\n\nThe theorem hypothesis gives `u<δ/8000≤κ/4`. If `a<κ/4`, the last two inequalities imply `9b≤a`, which contradicts the first inequality. If `b<κ/4`, they imply `a≤b`, which contradicts `e≥κb`. Hence `a,b≥κ/4≥δ/8000`. The polynomial from [P7] therefore has global agreement at least `δ/8000`. This is the sole incidence Cauchy–Schwarz loss.\n\n**[P9] (proved) Exact cubic reconstruction.** The dominant scales are\n\n`r=O(σp/δ)`,  `D=O(sqrt(dσp/δ))`,  `D=O(δp)`.\n\nThe first two give the interpolation degree; the last is independently demanded by identity extension, the `D/p` bad-incidence term, and lifting. Squaring the final comparison yields exactly `δ³=Ω(dσ/p)`. The resultant term `D²/p²` alone needs only `δ²=Ω(dσ/p)`, and mixing needs only `δ=Ω(p^−1/2)`; both are weaker here. For σ=1 this is the KTZ cubic exponent.\n\n**[P10] (conditional) Concentrated-carrier exponent.** If additionally `σ≤Aδ`, [P9] becomes `δ²=Ω(Ad/p)`, giving exponent `1/2`. Since every carrier has `σ≥δ`, this support-sensitive interpolation balance cannot exceed exponent `1/2`. This is not an unconditional improvement of the benchmark.\n\n**[P11] (proved) Modal occupancy lower bound.** For Theorem C choose all `p²` point values independently and uniformly. On a fixed line let `N_a` be the occupancy of value `a`, `M=max_a N_a`, and `Y=Σ_a 1[N_a=r]`. For one value,\n\n`Pr[N_a=r] = binom(p,r)p^(−r)(1−1/p)^(p−r) ≥ 1/(8r!)`.\n\nHere `r²≤p`, `(1−1/p)^p≥1/4`, and `r!≤r^r≤p^(1/4)`. Thus `μ=E[Y]≥p^(3/4)/8≥1`. For distinct values, the joint probability of both occupancies equaling `r` is at most `1/(r!)²`, at most 64 times the product of the lower bounds. Hence `E[Y²]≤μ+64μ²≤65μ²`. Cauchy–Schwarz, equivalently the zero-threshold Paley–Zygmund argument, gives `Pr[Y>0]≥1/65`, so `E[M]≥r/65`.\n\nGive each line a modal constant label. By linearity of expectation across lines—no line independence is asserted—the local agreement `A` satisfies `E[A]≥r/(65p)`.\n\n**[P12] (proved) Modal upper concentration.** A factorial-moment union bound gives\n\n`Pr[M≥s]≤p/s!≤p(e/s)^s`.\n\nFor `s0=ceil(4 log p/log log p)`, the tail sums to less than one and `E[M]≤s0+1≤25r`; hence `E[A]≤25r/p`. Changing one point value changes the modal count on only its `p+1` incident lines and changes `A` by at most `1/p²`. McDiarmid therefore gives\n\n`Pr[A>50r/p]≤exp(−1250r²)≤r/(520p)`.\n\nNo Markov inequality is used.\n\n**[P13] (proved) Global union bound and deterministic instance.** There are `p^N` formal total-degree-at-most-101 polynomials, with `N=5253`. For fixed `Q`, its agreement count with random `f` is `Bin(p²,1/p)`, of mean `p`. Chernoff gives\n\n`Pr[agreements(Q,f)≥2p]≤(e/4)^p`.\n\nUnion over all `p^N` polynomials gives `p^N(e/4)^p≤exp(−p/4)≤r/(520p)` under the stated lower bound on `p`. Let `G` be the event that all global agreements are below `2/p`, and `H={A≤50r/p}`. Since `0≤A≤1`,\n\n`E[A·1_{G∩H}] ≥ r/(65p)−r/(520p)−r/(520p) > r/(130p)`.\n\nSome deterministic table in `G∩H` therefore has all three bounds in Theorem C.\n\n**[P14] (refuted) Uniform exact-linear soundness.** Suppose constants `C,c>0` made `ε≥Cd/p` imply `Agr_d(f)≥cε` uniformly. Fix the legal ambient cap `d=101` and choose a sufficiently large prime with `r≥max{130·101C,260/c}`. Theorem C then has `ε≥C·101/p` but `Agr_101(f)<2/p<cε`, a contradiction. Thus the exact-linear statement is false. On the other hand, for each fixed `η>0`,\n\n`ε/(101/p)^(1−η) ≤ 50r/[101^(1−η)p^η] → 0`,\n\nso this construction does not refute a fixed-η target.\n\n**[P15] (proved) Near-p information set.** Choose distinct `a_0,…,a_d` and `b_0,…,b_d` and the triangular set `S={(a_i,b_j):i+j≤d}`. The Newton products `∏_{h<i}(X−a_h)∏_{k<j}(Y−b_k)` with `i+j≤d` form a triangular evaluation basis on `S`. Hence arbitrary prescribed values on all `|S|=(d+1)(d+2)/2` points extend to a total-degree-at-most-`d` polynomial. Applying this to `f|_S` proves Proposition D. In particular, the lower bound is `(p+1)/(2p)` at `d=p−1` and `5253/10609` at `d=101,p=103`.\n\n**[P16] (proved) Diffuse support need not concentrate.** Fix the legal ambient `d≥101`, take `f=0`, and on every line choose a degree-`d` label with `d` distinct prescribed parameter roots. Then `ε=d/p` and every line supports acceptance, so `σ=1`; nevertheless `Q=0` agrees globally everywhere. Thus local density does not imply `σ=O(ε)`, although this example is harmless for soundness.\n\n**[P17] (refuted as an obstruction) Concentrated good directions.** Let `f` be a product of `d+1` distinct homogeneous linear forms. In each of the corresponding `d+1` projective directions, every affine-line restriction loses its degree-`d+1` leading term and is a legal degree-`d` label. This gives local mass about `(d+1)/(p+1)`. But `Q=0` agrees on the union of the same `d+1` lines through the origin, a Θ(d/p) fraction. The attempted counterexample already contains the required global polynomial.\n\n**[P18] (refuted safety of omitting simplicity) Branch collision.** For odd `p` and legal ambient cap `d≥101`, `B=Z²−X²` is squarefree but its two legal branches `Q=X` and `Q=−X` meet at the origin, where `B_Z=0`. Agreement at that incidence cannot select a branch. Vertical-simple-root deletion is therefore logically necessary.\n\n**[P19] (refuted as an active obstruction) Inseparability.** A polynomial with vanishing `Z`-derivative must use positive `Z`-exponents divisible by `p`. Since the interpolant has weighted degree `D<p`, no such exponent occurs. Examples such as `Z^p−G` lie outside the interpolation space and do not obstruct the prime-field proof.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Scale or loss | Consequence |\n|---|---|---|\n| Carrier pruning | `<δ/50`, retained as `δ/4` | Constant only |\n| Selector probability | Hoeffding `e^(−k0/8)`, union over `p(p+1)` | No δ-power loss |\n| Selector size | Chebyshev; `r≤6400σp/δ` | One factor `σ/δ` |\n| Interpolation | `dim(V_D)≈D³/d` versus `rD` constraints | `D≈sqrt(dr)` |\n| Root budget | `D≤Θ(δp)` | `δ³=Ω(dσ/p)` |\n| Content/resultant deletion | `D/p + D²/p²` | Cubic plus a weaker quadratic gate |\n| Second pruning | `<δ/500` | Constant only |\n| Mixing | One Cauchy–Schwarz error `p^−1/2` | Weaker than cubic for `d≥101` |\n| Recovery | Component point density `δ/8000` | Linear global recovery |\n| Diffuse carrier | `σ=1` | Exponent `1/3` |\n| Concentrated carrier | `σ≤Aδ` | Conditional exponent `1/2` |\n| Modal occupancy | `r≈log p/(4 log log p)` | Local `Θ(r/p)` |\n| Polynomial union | `p^5253(e/4)^p` | Global `<2/p` |\n| Exact-linear claim | Ratio at most `260/r` | Tends to zero; exponent 1 with constant threshold is false |\n\nThere is no hidden Markov loss. The only probabilistic inequalities are the selector's Hoeffding, union, and Chebyshev bounds; the modal occupancy second moment, factorial union, and McDiarmid bound; and the global Chernoff union. The sole incidence Cauchy–Schwarz loss is the `p^−1/2` mixing error.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\nThe successful adversarial table is Theorem C: it is diffuse across lines and exploits the maximum occupancy among `p` symbols, not low characteristic or a small exceptional direction set. It proves that the campaign's possible sharp threshold cannot literally be a constant multiple of `d/p` with linear recovery.\n\nThe all-lines prescribed-root table [P16] shows why line-support concentration cannot be assumed. The homogeneous-direction construction [P17] fails because its zero set already supplies a global polynomial. The branch collision [P18] validates the simple-root deletion. The inseparable attempt [P19] is excluded by `D<p`. Proposition D handles `d` near `p`; it is a positive agreement baseline, not an obstruction.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- The field is exactly the prime field `F_p`; no extension-field descent is used.\n- The ambient degree always satisfies `101≤d<p`. Constant or linear objects appearing inside examples are legal labels or branches under that ambient cap; no test with parameter `d≤100` is analyzed.\n- Because `D<p`, the characteristic-pruned weighted monomial set equals the full weighted ball: every positive `Z`-exponent is strictly below `p`.\n- Lemma B rules out inseparable vertical factors after content removal. Absolute irreducibility is unnecessary.\n- KTZ's source proof uses a generic directional derivative. The replacement by `B_Z` is a new prime-field simplification and causes no exponent gain.\n- No discriminant is used. The resultant is invoked only for the proved coprime pair `(B,B_Z)`.\n- Division by `H` occurs only as an integral-domain inference on non-content lines. Hensel lifting divides only by a nonzero scalar `B_Z(x,f(x))`.\n- All interpolation constraints are coefficient identities, and every later root count uses distinct points or directions rather than multiplicity.\n- When `d` is near `p`, Theorem A's premise is vacuous because `σ≥δ` would force `p≥10^15d`; Proposition D supplies the appropriate direct check.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe general KTZ benchmark is not improved: the exponent `1/2` conclusion requires the additional hypothesis `σ=O(δ)`, and diffuse carriers can have `σ=1`. The constant `10^15` is deliberately conservative and is not claimed optimal.\n\nThe modal obstruction refutes a uniform constant-times-`d/p` trigger but not any fixed exponent `1−η`. It instead shows that an exponent-1 formulation must include a subpolynomial occupancy allowance, at least on the order of `log p/log log p` when `d=101`.\n\nThe current selector has an upper bound `O(σp/δ)`, whereas covering more than `k0/2` points on one line requires at least `Ω(δp)` distinct witness lines. Closing this gap demands a new combinatorial or algebraic idea. Every line contains \\(p\\) points and every point lies on \\(p+1\\) lines. Hence choosing a uniform line and then a uniform point on it is exactly uniform incident-pair sampling. For a point table \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\) and arbitrary line polynomials \\(P_L\\) of degree at most \\(d\\), write\n\\[\n\\epsilon=\\operatorname{Agr}_{\\rm LVP}(f,P)\n =\\Pr_{L,\\,x\\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)].\n\\]\nGlobal degree always means **total degree**. No axis-parallel or best-fit-only test is substituted.\n\nFor \\(1\\le d<p\\), set\n\\[\n\\operatorname{wdeg}(X^aY^bZ^i)=a+b+di.\n\\]\nWrite\n\\(B=\\sum_{i=0}^n b_i(X,Y)Z^i\\). The literature summaries were therefore used only for navigation.\n\n## Theorem\n\n### Theorem A (vertical separability and weighted resultant; proved here)\n\nLet \\(p\\) be prime, \\(1\\le d<p\\), and \\(D<p\\). Let\n\\[\nB(X,Y,Z)=\\sum_{i=0}^n b_i(X,Y)Z^i\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]\n\\]\nbe nonzero, squarefree, primitive in \\(Z\\), of positive \\(Z\\)-degree \\(n\\), and of \\((1,1,d)\\)-weighted degree at most \\(D\\). Then\n\\[\n\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1\n\\]\nand, for \\(R=\\operatorname{Res}_Z(B,B_Z)\\),\n\\[\nR\\ne0,\n\\qquad\n\\deg R\\le E:=(2n-1)D-dn^2\n\\le D^2/d-D.\n\\]\n\nIf \\(\\mathcal T\\) is any family of distinct affine lines carrying degree-at-most-\\(d\\) polynomials with\n\\(B(L(t),p_L(t))\\equiv0\\), then at most \\(E\\) lines also have\n\\(B_Z(L(t),p_L(t))\\equiv0\\). On every other line there are at most \\(D-d\\) points at which \\(B_Z(L(t),p_L(t))=0\\). Thus their normalized incidence loss is at most\n\\[\n\\frac{E}{p(p+1)}+\\frac{D-d}{p}.\n\\]\nIf one first removes the \\(Z\\)-content \\(H(X,Y)\\) from an interpolant of degree at most \\(D\\), the at most \\(D\\) content-trivial lines add only \\(D/[p(p+1)]\\).\n\n### Proposition B (thickened-line interpolation; proved here)\n\nLet \\(r\\) line graphs \\(\\Gamma_M\\) carry degree-at-most-\\(d\\) labels, let \\(s\\ge1\\), and let \\(W_D\\) be the full weighted-degree-at-most-\\(D\\) space. In affine coordinates \\((t,u)\\) with \\(M=\\{u=0\\}\\), put\n\\[\nI_M=(u,Z-p_M(t)).\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\n\\dim W_D=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\lfloor D/d\\rfloor}\\binom{D-dj+2}{2},\n\\]\nand the codimension of \\(I_M^s\\cap W_D\\) is at most\n\\[\nJ_s(D,d)=\\sum_{a+b<s}(D-a-db+1)_+.\n\\]\nConsequently a nonzero \\(A\\in W_D\\cap\\bigcap_M I_M^s\\) exists whenever\n\\(\\dim W_D>rJ_s(D,d)\\). For \\(D\\ge2d\\), it suffices that\n\\[\nD^2>16drs(s+1).\n\\]\nAt each distinct accepted crossing with a seed graph, the restriction to a target graph acquires a root of multiplicity at least \\(s\\); \\(N\\) distinct crossings force the target identity if \\(sN>D\\).\n\n### Theorem C (the legal \\(d=0\\) endpoint refutes the campaign statement)\n\nFor every prime \\(p\\ge e^{64}\\), set\n\\[\nk=\\left\\lfloor\\frac{\\log p}{4\\log\\log p}\\right\\rfloor.\n\\]\nThere exist \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\) and a degree-zero line table such that\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Agr}_{\\rm LVP}(f,P)\\ge \\frac{k}{256p},\n\\qquad\n\\max_{\\deg Q\\le0}\\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\\le\\frac2p.\n\\]\nThe global/local ratio is at most \\(512/k=o(1)\\). Therefore no absolute \\(c>0\\) can give global agreement at least \\(c\\epsilon\\) under the trigger \\(C(d/p)^\\alpha\\) for all \\(0\\le d<p\\), for any \\(\\alpha>0\\).\n\n## Proof\n\n**[P1, proved] Weighted consequences.** From weighted degree, \\(n\\le D/d<p\\) and \\(\\deg b_i\\le D-di\\). In particular \\(n\\) is nonzero in \\(\\mathbb F_p\\), so \\(B_Z\\) has \\(Z\\)-degree exactly \\(n-1\\). No derivative coefficient is divided by zero.\n\n**[P2, proved] Vertical coprimality.** Suppose an irreducible \\(C\\) divides both \\(B\\) and \\(B_Z\\), and write \\(B=CE\\). Squarefreeness gives \\(C\\nmid E\\). Modulo \\(C\\),\n\\[\n0\\equiv B_Z\\equiv C_ZE,\n\\]\nso \\(C\\mid C_Z\\); degree forces \\(C_Z=0\\). Since \\(\\deg C\\le D<p\\), every positive \\(Z\\)-exponent of \\(C\\) is below \\(p\\) and has nonzero derivative. Hence \\(C\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y]\\). Then \\(C\\) divides every \\(b_i\\), contradicting primitivity. Thus \\(\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1\\).\n\n**[P3, proved] Resultant degree.** The Sylvester determinant has \\(n-1\\) rows from \\(B\\) and \\(n\\) rows from \\(B_Z\\); every monomial in \\(R\\) therefore contains \\(2n-1\\) coefficient factors. Under \\(b_i\\mapsto\\lambda^i b_i\\), one has \\(B(Z)\\mapsto B(\\lambda Z)\\) and \\(B_Z(Z)\\mapsto\\lambda B_Z(\\lambda Z)\\), so the resultant scales by \\(\\lambda^{n(n-1)+n}=\\lambda^{n^2}\\). Every resultant monomial consequently has coefficient-index sum \\(n^2\\). Since \\(\\deg b_i\\le D-di\\),\n\\[\n\\deg R\\le(2n-1)D-dn^2.\n\\]\nCoprimality makes \\(R\\ne0\\). Finally,\n\\[\nD^2/d-D-E=(D-dn)^2/d\\ge0.\n\\]\n\n**[P4, proved] Exceptional lines and points.** If both \\(B\\) and \\(B_Z\\) vanish formally on \\(\\Gamma_L\\), then \\(R(L(t))\\equiv0\\). A nonzero bivariate polynomial of degree \\(E\\) can contain at most \\(E\\) distinct affine lines, because each line equation is a distinct irreducible factor. On a remaining line, \\(B_Z(L(t),p_L(t))\\) is nonzero and has degree at most \\(D-d\\), hence at most \\(D-d\\) roots. Dividing the line count by \\(p(p+1)\\) and the point count by \\(p\\) gives the asserted incidence loss. This uses neither a discriminant nor a union over derivative directions.\n\n**[P5, proved] Consequence for the KTZ algebraic stage.** KTZ writes \\(A=HB\\), with \\(H\\) the gcd of the \\(Z\\)-coefficients. Their minimum interpolant is squarefree and has \\(A_Z\\ne0\\); hence \\(B\\) is primitive, squarefree, and has positive \\(Z\\)-degree. Lemma 4.1 supplies \\(D<p\\). Theorem A therefore permits using \\(B_Z\\) directly in Section 5. The bad-line term improves from \\(D(D-1)/[p(p+1)]\\) to at most \\((D^2/d-D)/[p(p+1)]\\), and the per-line point term from \\(D/p\\) to \\((D-d)/p\\). Hensel lifting divides only by retained nonzero values of \\(B_Z\\).\n\n**[P6, proved] Why the exponent does not improve.** KTZ Lemma 3.2 and Section 4 give \\(|\\mathcal R|=\\Theta(p/\\epsilon)\\) and \\(D=\\Theta(\\sqrt{d|\\mathcal R|})=\\Theta(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\). Formal extension, post-deletion minimum degree, and lifting require \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\). Squaring and rearranging gives\n\\[\n\\frac{dp}{\\epsilon}=O(\\epsilon^2p^2)\n\\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p).\n\\]\nThe new exceptional-line term is \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\), but the remaining point term is\n\\((D-d)/p=\\Theta(\\sqrt{d/(\\epsilon p)})\\); asking it to be \\(O(\\epsilon)\\) gives the same cubic inequality.\n\n**[P7, proved] Thickened-line dimension count.** The filtered change of variables \\((X,Y,Z)\\leftrightarrow(t,u,Z-p_M(t))\\) preserves weighted degree. Modulo \\(I_M^s\\), the surviving basis monomials are\n\\[\nt^c u^a(Z-p_M(t))^b,\n\\qquad a+b<s,\\quad c+a+db\\le D,\n\\]\nwhich gives \\(J_s(D,d)\\). Codimensions subadd over \\(r\\) seed graphs. For \\(D\\ge2d\\), the terms \\(0\\le j\\le D/(2d)\\) show \\(\\dim W_D\\ge D^3/(16d)\\), while \\(J_s(D,d)\\le s(s+1)D\\). The displayed sufficient condition follows.\n\n**[P8, proved] Multiplicity propagation and its simple-root obstruction.** At a crossing of distinct base lines, both generators of \\(I_M\\) vanish to order at least one on the target graph. Membership in \\(I_M^s\\) therefore gives Hasse root multiplicity at least \\(s\\); \\(N\\) distinct points contribute total multiplicity at least \\(sN\\). Repeated sampled lines through the same point count only once. However, for \\(s\\ge2\\), \\(A_Z\\in I_M^{s-1}\\), so every seed root is vertically degenerate. If \\(A=HB\\) and \\(H\\) is nontrivial neither identically zero on \\(M\\), then \\(A_Z=HB_Z\\) still forces \\(B_Z\\) to vanish formally there. Plain multiplicity interpolation therefore cannot feed the simple-root Newton--Hensel step.\n\n**[P9, proved] Multiplicity exponent ledger.** At KTZ scale, \\(r\\le6400p/\\epsilon\\). If \\(\\epsilon p\\ge200\\), Lemma 3.2 supplies more than \\(N=\\epsilon p/400\\) distinct covered points per target line. The sufficient interpolation inequality and propagation inequality are\n\\[\nD^2>16drs(s+1),\\qquad D<sN.\n\\]\nAn interval certified by these worst-case bounds is obtained only under\n\\[\n\\epsilon^3>16{,}384{,}000{,}000\\frac{s+1}{s}\\frac d p.\n\\]\nThus \\(s\\) cancels up to \\((s+1)/s\\), and there is no exponent gain.\n\n**[P10, proved] Occupancy on one line.** Choose \\(f(x)\\) independently and uniformly in \\(\\mathbb F_p\\). On a fixed line let \\(N_a\\) be the occupancy of color \\(a\\), \\(M=\\max_aN_a\\), and \\(Y=|\\{a:N_a=k\\}|\\). For \\(p\\ge e^{64}\\), \\(k!\\le k^k\\le p^{1/4}\\), and\n\\[\n\\frac1{8k!}\\le\\Pr[N_a=k]\\le\\frac1{k!},\n\\qquad\n\\Pr[N_a=N_b=k]\\le\\frac1{k!^2}\\quad(a\\ne b).\n\\]\nThe lower bound uses\n\\(\\binom pkp^{-k}\\ge1/(2k!)\\) and \\((1-1/p)^p\\ge1/4\\). Hence\n\\[\n\\mathbb EY\\ge\\frac{p}{8k!},\n\\qquad\n\\mathbb EY^2\\le\\frac p{k!}+\\frac{p^2}{k!^2}\n \\le\\frac{2p^2}{k!^2}.\n\\]\nThe second-moment/Cauchy--Schwarz inequality loses the explicit factor \\(1/128\\):\n\\(\\Pr[Y>0]\\ge(\\mathbb EY)^2/\\mathbb EY^2\\ge1/128\\). Thus \\(\\mathbb EM\\ge k/128\\).\n\n**[P11, proved] Global balance and simultaneous existence.** For deterministic \\(f\\), let \\(A(f)\\) be the acceptance obtained by choosing a modal constant on every line. Linearity of expectation—no independence between lines—is enough to give \\(\\mathbb EA(f)\\ge k/(128p)\\). For a global color class \\(X_a=|f^{-1}(a)|\\sim\\operatorname{Bin}(p^2,1/p)\\), Chernoff gives \\(\\Pr[X_a>2p]\\le(e/4)^p\\). The only union bound in this proof is over the \\(p\\) colors:\n\\[\n\\Pr[\\max_aX_a>2p]\\le p(e/4)^p\\le\\frac{k}{256p}.\n\\]\nSince \\(0\\le A\\le1\\), restricting the expectation to the balance event leaves at least \\(k/(256p)\\). Some balanced \\(f\\) attains that value. No Markov loss is used.\n\n**[P12, proved] Refutation at \\(d=0\\).** Choose each \\(P_L\\) to be a modal color. Its acceptance is \\(A(f)\\). Every total-degree-zero polynomial is constant, so its agreement is at most \\(2/p\\). Given proposed absolute \\(C,c>0\\), choose a sufficiently large prime with \\(k>512/c\\). The premise \\(\\epsilon\\ge C(0/p)^\\alpha=0\\) holds, but global agreement is less than \\(c\\epsilon\\). This refutes the literal cubic benchmark and, for every fixed \\(0<\\eta<1\\), the literal \\((d/p)^{1-\\eta}\\) target.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input | Loss | Output |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| KTZ seed selection | local agreement \\(\\epsilon\\) | \\(|\\mathcal R|=\\Theta(p/\\epsilon)\\) | one factor \\(\\epsilon^{-1}\\) |\n| Ordinary interpolation | \\(|V_D|=\\Theta(D^3/d)\\), \\(|\\mathcal R|(D+1)\\) constraints | \\(D^2=\\Theta(d|\\mathcal R|)\\) | \\(D=\\Theta(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\) |\n| Extension/lifting | \\(D\\) versus \\(\\Theta(\\epsilon p)\\) roots/lines | require \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\) | \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\) |\n| New vertical resultant | \\(n\\le D/d\\) | at most \\(D^2/d-D\\) bad lines | normalized \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\) at KTZ scale |\n| Remaining bad points | degree \\(D-d\\) on each nonbad line | \\((D-d)/p\\) | still forces \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\) |\n| Multiplicity \\(s\\) | interpolation cost \\(\\Theta(s^2)\\), root credit \\(s\\) | \\(D\\asymp s\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon}\\), allowance \\(s\\epsilon p\\) | \\(s\\) cancels; exponent \\(1/3\\) |\n| Degree zero | \\(k=\\Theta(\\log p/\\log\\log p)\\) | local \\(\\ge k/(256p)\\), global \\(\\le2/p\\) | global/local \\(\\le512/k=o(1)\\) |\n\nKTZ's Lemma 3.2 also uses a Chernoff bound, a union bound over all affine lines, and Chebyshev for \\(|\\mathcal R|\\); these produce the displayed constants but no additional power of \\(\\epsilon\\) beyond \\(|\\mathcal R|=O(p/\\epsilon)\\). Their point-line Cauchy--Schwarz mixing error is \\(1/\\sqrt{p+1}\\), required to be at most \\(\\epsilon/8000\\); for \\(d\\ge1\\) this is dominated by a sufficiently large cubic trigger. These are quoted source losses, not silently suppressed steps in the new proof.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Adversarial table, successful:** the random balanced coloring with modal constant line labels proves Theorem C. Randomness is only a probabilistic existence proof; the resulting table is deterministic.\n2. **Concentrated good direction, not a vanishing-ratio example:** for \\(d=0\\), take \\(f(x,y)=x\\). The \\(p\\) vertical lines accept everywhere with their constant labels; every other line has one occurrence of each value. The modal table has \\(\\epsilon=2/(p+1)\\), while the best global constant has agreement \\(1/p\\), a ratio \\((p+1)/(2p)>1/2\\).\n3. **Inseparability boundary, successful algebraic obstruction:** for \\(d=1,D=p\\), \\(B=Z^p-X\\) is primitive and squarefree (indeed irreducible by Eisenstein at \\(X\\)), but \\(B_Z=0\\). Thus \\(D<p\\) cannot simply be dropped.\n4. **Multiplicity, refuted as a plug-in improvement:** the factor \\(s\\) cancels in the exponent, and \\(s\\ge2\\) destroys simple vertical roots on every seed graph.\n5. **\\(d\\) near \\(p\\), no counterexample claimed:** every line table can interpolate arbitrary line values at \\(d=p-1\\), but this does not replace total degree by individual degree and does not itself contradict constant global agreement. For any quoted threshold constant \\(C>1\\), the premise is already vacuous when \\(d/p>C^{-3}\\) for the cubic trigger.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- Theorem A uses primality through characteristic \\(p\\); the same argument works over perfect characteristic-\\(p\\) fields, but no extension-field claim is made.\n- The deductions \\(n<p\\) and \\(C_Z=0\\Rightarrow C\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y]\\) use \\(D<p\\). The explicit \\(Z^p-X\\) example audits sharpness.\n- No discriminant is divided by or assumed nonzero. The nonzero resultant follows from the proved coprimality.\n- No irreducibility of \\(B\\) is assumed. Squarefreeness is used factor by factor; primitivity excludes an \\(X,Y\\)-only common factor.\n- Content division is safe in the integral domain \\(\\mathbb F_p[t]\\). Hensel division occurs only after retaining \\(B_Z(x,f(x))\\ne0\\).\n- The multiplicity proof uses ideal powers/Hasse multiplicity. Ordinary derivatives would be invalid for orders reaching \\(p\\), since \\((t^p)'=0\\).\n- Several lines through one point provide one distinct root, not several. Parallel lines provide no crossing. Both concentration modes are explicitly excluded from multiplicity overcounting.\n- At \\(d=0\\), the weighted monomial count \\(D^3/(64d)\\) is undefined and the \\(Z\\)-weight is zero; this exactly matches the endpoint missed by the positive-degree algebraic proof.\n- For the smallest primes, the asymptotic counterexample is not asserted. Exhaustive checks give ratios \\(3/4\\) at \\(p=2\\) and \\(4/7\\) at \\(p=3\\). At \\(p=2,d=1\\), Theorem A only permits \\(D=1\\), where vertical differentiation is ordinary and separable.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThe vertical-resultant lemma is a genuine prime-field simplification and improves one quantitative deletion term, but it leaves the cubic bottleneck intact. Thus `benchmark_improved=false`; the durable target first needs the correction \\(1\\le d<p\\), or a trigger involving \\(d+1\\).\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nThere are exactly \\(p(p+1)\\) affine lines in \\(\\mathbb F_p^2\\). Every line contains \\(p\\) points and every point lies on \\(p+1\\) lines. Hence choosing a uniform line and then a uniform point on it is exactly uniform incident-pair sampling. For a point table \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\) and arbitrary line polynomials \\(P_L\\) of degree at most \\(d\\), write\n\\[\n\\epsilon=\\operatorname{Agr}_{\\rm LVP}(f,P)\n =\\Pr_{L,\\,x\\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)].\n\\]\nGlobal degree always means **total degree**. No axis-parallel or best-fit-only test is substituted.\n\nFor \\(1\\le d<p\\), set\n\\[\n\\operatorname{wdeg}(X^aY^bZ^i)=a+b+di.\n\\]\nWrite \\(B=\\sum_{i=0}^n b_i(X,Y)Z^i\\). A line-polynomial graph is\n\\(\\Gamma_L=\\{(L(t),p_L(t)):t\\in\\mathbb F_p\\}\\).\n\nThe case \\(d=0\\) is treated separately because the above weight gives \\(Z\\) weight zero and the unrestricted weighted interpolation space is infinite-dimensional.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe controlling source is [Kominers--Thaler--Zheng, ECCC TR26-147, revision 1](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download). The literature summaries were therefore used only for navigation.\n\n## Theorem\n\n### Theorem A (vertical separability and weighted resultant)\n\nLet \\(p\\) be prime, \\(1\\le d<p\\), and \\(D<p\\). Let\n\\[\nB(X,Y,Z)=\\sum_{i=0}^n b_i(X,Y)Z^i\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]\n\\]\nbe nonzero, squarefree, primitive in \\(Z\\), of positive \\(Z\\)-degree \\(n\\), and of \\((1,1,d)\\)-weighted degree at most \\(D\\). Then\n\\[\n\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1\n\\]\nand, for \\(R=\\operatorname{Res}_Z(B,B_Z)\\),\n\\[\nR\\ne0,\n\\qquad\n\\deg R\\le E:=(2n-1)D-dn^2\n\\le D^2/d-D.\n\\]\n\nIf \\(\\mathcal T\\) is any family of distinct affine lines carrying degree-at-most-\\(d\\) polynomials with \\(B(L(t),p_L(t))\\equiv0\\), then at most \\(E\\) lines also have \\(B_Z(L(t),p_L(t))\\equiv0\\). On every other line there are at most \\(D-d\\) points at which \\(B_Z(L(t),p_L(t))=0\\). Their normalized incidence loss is at most\n\\[\n\\frac{E}{p(p+1)}+\\frac{D-d}{p}.\n\\]\nIf one first removes the \\(Z\\)-content \\(H(X,Y)\\) from an interpolant of degree at most \\(D\\), the at most \\(D\\) content-trivial lines add \\(D/[p(p+1)]\\).\n\n### Proposition B (thickened-line interpolation)\n\nLet \\(r\\) line graphs \\(\\Gamma_M\\) carry degree-at-most-\\(d\\) labels, let \\(s\\ge1\\), and let \\(W_D\\) be the full weighted-degree-at-most-\\(D\\) space. In affine coordinates \\((t,u)\\) with \\(M=\\{u=0\\}\\), put\n\\[\nI_M=(u,Z-p_M(t)).\n\\]\nThen\n\\[\n\\dim W_D=\\sum_{j=0}^{\\lfloor D/d\\rfloor}\\binom{D-dj+2}{2},\n\\]\nand the codimension of \\(I_M^s\\cap W_D\\) is at most\n\\[\nJ_s(D,d)=\\sum_{a+b<s}(D-a-db+1)_+.\n\\]\nConsequently, a nonzero \\(A\\in W_D\\cap\\bigcap_M I_M^s\\) exists whenever \\(\\dim W_D>rJ_s(D,d)\\). For \\(D\\ge2d\\), it suffices that\n\\[\nD^2>16drs(s+1).\n\\]\nAt each distinct accepted crossing with a seed graph, the restriction to a target graph acquires a root of multiplicity at least \\(s\\); \\(N\\) distinct crossings force the target identity if \\(sN>D\\).\n\n### Theorem C (the legal d=0 endpoint refutes the campaign statement)\n\nFor every prime \\(p\\ge e^{64}\\), set\n\\[\nk=\\left\\lfloor\\frac{\\log p}{4\\log\\log p}\\right\\rfloor.\n\\]\nThere exist \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\) and a degree-zero line table such that\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Agr}_{\\rm LVP}(f,P)\\ge \\frac{k}{256p},\n\\qquad\n\\max_{\\deg Q\\le0}\\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\\le\\frac2p.\n\\]\nThe global/local ratio is at most \\(512/k=o(1)\\). Therefore no absolute \\(c>0\\) can give global agreement at least \\(c\\epsilon\\) under the trigger \\(C(d/p)^\\alpha\\) for all \\(0\\le d<p\\), for any \\(\\alpha>0\\).\n\n## Proof\n\n**[P1, proved] Weighted consequences.** Weighted degree gives \\(n\\le D/d<p\\) and \\(\\deg b_i\\le D-di\\). In particular, \\(n\\) is nonzero in \\(\\mathbb F_p\\), so \\(B_Z\\) has \\(Z\\)-degree exactly \\(n-1\\). No derivative coefficient is divided by zero.\n\n**[P2, proved] Vertical coprimality.** Suppose an irreducible \\(C\\) divides both \\(B\\) and \\(B_Z\\), and write \\(B=CE\\). Squarefreeness gives \\(C\\nmid E\\). Modulo \\(C\\),\n\\[\n0\\equiv B_Z\\equiv C_ZE,\n\\]\nso \\(C\\mid C_Z\\); degree forces \\(C_Z=0\\). Since \\(\\deg C\\le D<p\\), every positive \\(Z\\)-exponent of \\(C\\) is below \\(p\\) and has nonzero derivative. Hence \\(C\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y]\\). Then \\(C\\) divides every \\(b_i\\), contradicting primitivity. Thus \\(\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1\\).\n\n**[P3, proved] Resultant degree.** The Sylvester determinant has \\(n-1\\) rows from \\(B\\) and \\(n\\) rows from \\(B_Z\\); every monomial in \\(R\\) therefore contains \\(2n-1\\) coefficient factors. Under \\(b_i\\mapsto\\lambda^i b_i\\), one has \\(B(Z)\\mapsto B(\\lambda Z)\\) and \\(B_Z(Z)\\mapsto\\lambda B_Z(\\lambda Z)\\), so the resultant scales by \\(\\lambda^{n(n-1)+n}=\\lambda^{n^2}\\). Every resultant monomial consequently has coefficient-index sum \\(n^2\\). Since \\(\\deg b_i\\le D-di\\),\n\\[\n\\deg R\\le(2n-1)D-dn^2.\n\\]\nCoprimality makes \\(R\\ne0\\). Finally,\n\\[\nD^2/d-D-E=(D-dn)^2/d\\ge0.\n\\]\n\n**[P4, proved] Exceptional lines and points.** If both \\(B\\) and \\(B_Z\\) vanish formally on \\(\\Gamma_L\\), then \\(R(L(t))\\equiv0\\). A nonzero bivariate polynomial of degree \\(E\\) can contain at most \\(E\\) distinct affine lines, because each line equation is a distinct irreducible factor. On a remaining line, \\(B_Z(L(t),p_L(t))\\) is nonzero and has degree at most \\(D-d\\), hence at most \\(D-d\\) roots. Dividing the line count by \\(p(p+1)\\) and the point count by \\(p\\) gives the asserted incidence loss. This uses neither a discriminant nor a union over derivative directions.\n\n**[P5, proved] Consequence for the KTZ algebraic stage.** KTZ writes \\(A=HB\\), with \\(H\\) the gcd of the \\(Z\\)-coefficients. Their minimum interpolant is squarefree and has \\(A_Z\\ne0\\); hence \\(B\\) is primitive, squarefree, and has positive \\(Z\\)-degree. Lemma 4.1 supplies \\(D<p\\). Theorem A therefore permits using \\(B_Z\\) directly in Section 5. The bad-line term improves from \\(D(D-1)/[p(p+1)]\\) to at most \\((D^2/d-D)/[p(p+1)]\\), and the per-line point term from \\(D/p\\) to \\((D-d)/p\\). Hensel lifting divides only by retained nonzero values of \\(B_Z\\).\n\n**[P6, proved] Why the exponent does not improve.** KTZ Lemma 3.2 and Section 4 give \\(|\\mathcal R|=\\Theta(p/\\epsilon)\\) and \\(D=\\Theta(\\sqrt{d|\\mathcal R|})=\\Theta(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\). Formal extension, post-deletion minimum degree, and lifting require \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\). Squaring and rearranging gives\n\\[\n\\frac{dp}{\\epsilon}=O(\\epsilon^2p^2)\n\\quad\\Longleftrightarrow\\quad\n\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p).\n\\]\nThe new exceptional-line term is \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\), but the remaining point term is \\((D-d)/p=\\Theta(\\sqrt{d/(\\epsilon p)})\\); asking it to be \\(O(\\epsilon)\\) gives the same cubic inequality.\n\n**[P7, proved] Thickened-line dimension count.** The filtered change of variables \\((X,Y,Z)\\leftrightarrow(t,u,Z-p_M(t))\\) preserves weighted degree. Modulo \\(I_M^s\\), the surviving basis monomials are\n\\[\nt^c u^a(Z-p_M(t))^b,\n\\qquad a+b<s,\\quad c+a+db\\le D,\n\\]\nwhich gives \\(J_s(D,d)\\). Codimensions subadd over \\(r\\) seed graphs. For \\(D\\ge2d\\), the terms \\(0\\le j\\le D/(2d)\\) show \\(\\dim W_D\\ge D^3/(16d)\\), while \\(J_s(D,d)\\le s(s+1)D\\). The displayed sufficient condition follows.\n\n**[P8, proved] Multiplicity propagation and its simple-root obstruction.** At a crossing of distinct base lines, both generators of \\(I_M\\) vanish to order at least one on the target graph. Membership in \\(I_M^s\\) therefore gives Hasse root multiplicity at least \\(s\\); \\(N\\) distinct points contribute total multiplicity at least \\(sN\\). Repeated sampled lines through the same point count only once. However, for \\(s\\ge2\\), \\(A_Z\\in I_M^{s-1}\\), so every seed root is vertically degenerate. If \\(A=HB\\) and \\(H\\) is not identically zero on \\(M\\), then \\(A_Z=HB_Z\\) still forces \\(B_Z\\) to vanish formally there. Plain multiplicity interpolation therefore cannot feed the simple-root Newton--Hensel step.\n\n**[P9, proved] Multiplicity exponent ledger.** At KTZ scale, \\(r\\le6400p/\\epsilon\\). If \\(\\epsilon p\\ge200\\), Lemma 3.2 supplies more than \\(N=\\epsilon p/400\\) distinct covered points per target line. This note isolates the algebraic obstruction left after introducing absolute factorization and discriminant curves into the affine line-versus-point test. First, an \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-irreducible auxiliary factor with \\(k\\ge2\\) absolute factors supports at most \\(\\delta^2/(dk^2)\\le\\delta^2/(4d)\\) polynomial graph lines; this follows from Frobenius conjugacy and a weighted resultant. Second, for a fixed factor, all ramified accepted lifts that are smooth on the auxiliary hypersurface contribute at most \\(p^2\\) incidences, hence normalized loss at most \\(1/(p+1)\\). Thus geometric reducibility and smooth ramification are not the cubic bottleneck.\n\nThe obstruction is the singular lifted locus. For every \\(101\\le d\\le p-2\\), an explicit minimum-weight, primitive, squarefree, absolutely irreducible polynomial \\(B=XZ+H(Y)\\) of weighted degree \\(D=d+1<p\\) has a smooth absolutely irreducible raw-resultant curve \\(X=0\\), supports more than \\(D\\) fully accepted graph lines, and has no total-degree-\\(d\\) polynomial root matching all those labels. At \\((p,d)=(103,101)\\), the construction contains 5,253 fully accepted lines. This is a proved obstruction to a proof architecture, not a counterexample to soundness and not an exponent improvement.\n\n## Test and Notation\n\nThere are \\(p(p+1)\\) affine lines in \\(\\mathbb F_p^2\\). A line table assigns to each line \\(L\\) one univariate polynomial \\(P_L\\) of degree at most \\(d\\), interpreted in any affine parameter on \\(L\\). For a point table \\(f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p\\),\n\\[\n\\epsilon=\\Pr_{L,x\\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)]\n=\\frac{\\#\\{(L,x):x\\in L,\\ P_L(x)=f(x)\\}}{p^2(p+1)}.\n\\]\nLine sampling and then point sampling are both uniform. A global polynomial always means one \\(Q\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y]\\) of total degree at most \\(d\\).\n\nGive \\(X,Y,Z\\) weights \\((1,1,d)\\). Write \\(\\operatorname{wdeg}B\\) for weighted degree and \\(\\deg_ZB\\) for vertical degree. A graph identity means the formal polynomial identity\n\\[\nB(L(t),P_L(t))\\equiv0\\quad\\text{in }\\mathbb F_p[t],\n\\]\nnot merely equality as functions on \\(\\mathbb F_p\\). A graph incidence is ramified when \\(B_Z(x,P_L(x))=0\\).\n\nAuxiliary symbols are as follows: \\(D\\) is an interpolation weight; \\(\\delta,r,k\\) are respectively the weight, vertical degree, and number of absolute factors of one \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-irreducible factor; \\(s=\\lfloor(d+1)/2\\rfloor\\) and \\(e=d+1-2s\\in\\{0,1\\}\\) occur in the explicit construction.\n\n## Prior Results\n\nThe quoted benchmark is Kominers–Thaler–Zheng Theorem 1.1: absolute constants \\(C,c>0\\) satisfy\n\\[\n\\epsilon\\ge C(d/p)^{1/3}\n\\quad\\Longrightarrow\\quad\n\\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\\ge c\\epsilon\n\\]\nfor some total-degree-\\(d\\) polynomial \\(Q\\); their bivariate proof gives \\(c=1/8000\\). Their Lemma 4.1 uses\n\\[\nD=16\\bigl(\\lfloor\\sqrt{d|\\mathcal R|}\\rfloor+1\\bigr),\n\\qquad |\\mathcal R|\\le6400p/\\epsilon.\n\\]\nThe familiar chain \\(D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\) and \\(D=O(\\epsilon p)\\), hence \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\), is this note's reconstruction from the proof, not a separately quoted KTZ theorem. See the [KTZ Revision 1 primary text](https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/147/revision/1/download/).\n\nHarsha–Kumar–Saptharishi–Sudan Definitions/Lemmas 2.5–2.10 use the raw resultant \\(\\operatorname{Res}_Z(A,A_Z)\\) as their \\(Z\\)-discriminant, and Lemma 3.1 requires a simple lifted root for global lifting. See the [HKSS primary text](https://arxiv.org/html/2311.12752v1). Arora–Sudan Theorem 34 bounds bad affine specializations of an absolutely irreducible polynomial, while Lemma 35 and Corollary 36 use discriminants under a separability hypothesis; see the [journal paper](https://people.csail.mit.edu/madhu/papers/1997/arora-journ.pdf).\n\nFor plane curves, Aubry–Perret Corollary 2.5 proves\n\\[\n|\\#C(\\mathbb F_p)-(p+1)|\\le(r-1)(r-2)\\sqrt p\n\\]\nfor an absolutely irreducible projective plane curve of degree \\(r\\); see the [primary paper](https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/~perret/Fichiers/Scan-Weil.Singulier.pdf). Cafure–Matera Lemma 2.3 bounds rational points on an \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-irreducible but non-absolutely-irreducible curve; see the [primary text](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0405302v1). Neither point theorem controls how many graph directions pass through one lifted singular point.\n\nIn the active campaign corpus, researcher-0002 is the only accepted prior submission; its exponent-\\(1/2\\) consequence remains conditional on a small-component hypothesis. Researchers 0001 and 0004 require revision. Researcher-0003 was rejected because its headline theorem omitted essential interpolation hypotheses, although its verifier accepted the weighted-resultant calculation used below. To avoid inheriting the rejected statement, that calculation is proved again in [P2].\n\n## Theorem\n\n**Theorem 1 (purification and singular-lift dichotomy).** Let \\(p\\) be prime and \\(101\\le d<p\\).\n\n1. **Frobenius purification.** Let \\(C\\in\\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]\\) be irreducible and \\(Z\\)-dependent, with weighted degree \\(\\delta\\), vertical degree \\(r\\), and \\(k\\ge2\\) absolute factors. If \\(\\mathcal T\\) is a family of distinct affine \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-lines with degree-at-most-\\(d\\) labels satisfying \\(C(L,P_L)\\equiv0\\), then\n   \\[\n   |\\mathcal T|\\le\\frac{2r\\delta-dr^2}{k^2}\n   \\le\\frac{\\delta^2}{dk^2}\n   \\le\\frac{\\delta^2}{4d}.\n   \\]\n   Consequently, for any primitive auxiliary polynomial of weight at most \\(D\\), all graph lines supported on geometrically reducible \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-factors number at most \\(D^2/(4d)\\).\n\n2. **Smooth ramification sparsity.** Fix one polynomial \\(B\\) and a graph-line family. If every ramified accepted lift \\(w=(x,f(x))\\) under consideration is smooth on \\(B=0\\), then their total number of accepted incidences is at most \\(p^2\\), giving normalized loss at most \\(1/(p+1)\\).\n\n3. **Linear regime.** If \\(d\\le D<2d\\) and \\(B\\) is primitive, \\(Z\\)-dependent, and of weight at most \\(D\\), then\n   \\[\n   B=a(X,Y)Z+b(X,Y),\\qquad\n   \\deg a\\le D-d,\n   \\quad \\deg b\\le D,\n   \\quad \\gcd(a,b)=1.\n   \\]\n   It is absolutely irreducible. Its ramified base set has at most \\(D(D-d)\\) points, no graph line is identically ramified, and deletion of all ramified base vertices costs at most \\(D(D-d)/p^2\\).\n\n4. **Sharp singular construction.** Suppose further that \\(d\\le p-2\\). Put \\(D=d+1\\), \\(s=\\lfloor(d+1)/2\\rfloor\\), and \\(e=d+1-2s\\). Choose distinct \\(c_1,\\ldots,c_s\\in\\mathbb F_p\\); if \\(e=1\\), choose \\(b\\notin\\{c_j\\}\\), and set\n   \\[\n   H(Y)=\\prod_{j=1}^s(Y-c_j)^2\\,(Y-b)^e,\n   \\qquad B(X,Y,Z)=XZ+H(Y).\n   \\]\n   Then \\(B\\) is a minimum-weight primitive, squarefree, absolutely irreducible graph interpolant of weight \\(D<p\\). There is a fully specified point/line table containing\n   \\[\n   sp>D\n   \\]\n   fully accepted lines, of line measure \\(s/(p+1)\\), with exactly one ramified accepted point per selected line. Their normalized ramified mass is \\(s/[p(p+1)]\\). The raw resultant is the smooth absolutely irreducible plane curve \\(X=0\\), but no total-degree-at-most-\\(d\\) polynomial restricts to all selected labels.\n\nNo part asserts a stronger soundness exponent or bounds the best global agreement for the explicit table.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n### [P1] Vertical separability — proved\n\nLet a squarefree polynomial \\(B\\), primitive in \\(Z\\), have weighted degree \\(\\delta<dp\\). Then \\(\\deg_ZB<p\\). If an irreducible factor \\(C\\) divided both \\(B\\) and \\(B_Z\\), squarefreeness would imply \\(C\\mid C_Z\\), so \\(C_Z=0\\). In characteristic \\(p\\), all its \\(Z\\)-exponents would then be multiples of \\(p\\). Since \\(\\deg_ZC<p\\), it would be independent of \\(Z\\), contradicting primitivity. Hence \\(\\gcd(B,B_Z)=1\\).\n\nThe strict threshold is necessary: \\(Z^p-X\\) has weighted degree \\(dp\\), is primitive, squarefree, smooth, and absolutely irreducible, but its \\(Z\\)-derivative is zero.\n\n### [P2] Weighted resultant line count — proved\n\nLet coprime \\(U,V\\) have weights \\(u,v\\) and vertical degrees \\(r_0,s_0\\). Their nonzero resultant \\(R=\\operatorname{Res}_Z(U,V)\\) has ordinary \\((X,Y)\\)-degree at most\n\\[\ns_0u+r_0v-dr_0s_0.\n\\]\nIndeed, every resultant monomial contains \\(s_0\\) coefficients of \\(U\\), \\(r_0\\) coefficients of \\(V\\), and total vertical-index weight \\(r_0s_0\\). Since the coefficient of \\(Z^i\\) in a weight-\\(u\\) polynomial has degree at most \\(u-di\\), the displayed bound follows term by term.\n\nIf both \\(U(L,P_L)\\) and \\(V(L,P_L)\\) vanish formally, then \\(R\\) vanishes identically on the base line \\(L\\). Its line equation divides \\(R\\). A nonzero bivariate polynomial of degree \\(E\\) has at most \\(E\\) distinct affine-line factors, proving the graph-line bound.\n\n### [P3] Frobenius purification — proved\n\nOver \\(\\overline{\\mathbb F}_p\\), Frobenius acts transitively on the \\(k\\) absolute factors of the \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-irreducible polynomial \\(C\\). Every factor has weight \\(\\delta/k\\) and vertical degree \\(r/k\\). If one factor vanishes on an \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-defined graph, applying Frobenius to that formal identity shows that every conjugate vanishes there. Two distinct conjugates are coprime, so [P2] gives\n\\[\n|\\mathcal T|\n\\le 2\\frac r k\\frac\\delta k-d\\left(\\frac r k\\right)^2\n=\\frac{2r\\delta-dr^2}{k^2}.\n\\]\nCompleting the square gives \\(2r\\delta-dr^2\\le\\delta^2/d\\), and \\(k\\ge2\\) gives the final \\(\\delta^2/(4d)\\) bound.\n\n### [P4] Union loss and sharpness — proved\n\nPrimitivity excludes base-only irreducible factors. Factor a primitive \\(B\\) over \\(\\mathbb F_p\\), assign each supported graph line to one factor, and apply [P3] to the geometrically reducible factors. If their weights are \\(\\delta_i\\), then\n\\[\n\\sum_i\\frac{\\delta_i^2}{4d}\n\\le\\frac{(\\sum_i\\delta_i)^2}{4d}\n\\le\\frac{D^2}{4d}.\n\\]\nThis is the sole union loss.\n\nThe constant is sharp. If \\(p>2d\\), choose a nonsquare \\(\\nu\\in\\mathbb F_p\\) and let \\(H_0\\) be the product of \\(d\\) distinct affine-line equations. Then\n\\[\nC=Z^2-\\nu H_0^2\n\\]\nis irreducible over \\(\\mathbb F_p\\), has \\(k=2\\), \\(r=2\\), and \\(\\delta=2d\\). It contains exactly the \\(d\\) base lines of \\(H_0\\) with label zero. If another graph existed, \\(q_L^2=\\nu H_0(L)^2\\) would make the nonsquare constant \\(\\nu\\) a square in \\(\\mathbb F_p(t)\\), which is impossible.\n\n### [P5] Smooth ramification sparsity — proved\n\nAt a ramified accepted lift \\(w=(x,f(x))\\), a formal graph identity along a line with direction \\(v_L\\) yields, by the chain rule,\n\\[\nB_X(w)v_{L,1}+B_Y(w)v_{L,2}+B_Z(w)P_L'(x)=0.\n\\]\nRamification removes the last term. Smoothness of \\(w\\) and \\(B_Z(w)=0\\) imply \\((B_X,B_Y)(w)\\ne(0,0)\\), whose kernel is one projective direction. Through \\(x\\) there is exactly one affine line of that direction. Thus each of the \\(p^2\\) base points supplies at most one such accepted edge. Division by a derivative is not used.\n\n### [P6] Linear-in-Z regime — proved\n\nIf \\(D<2d\\), positive vertical degree and the weight constraint force\n\\[\nB=aZ+b,\n\\quad \\deg a\\le D-d,\n\\quad \\deg b\\le D.\n\\]\nPrimitivity says \\(\\gcd(a,b)=1\\), and Gauss's lemma makes this primitive linear polynomial absolutely irreducible. A base point admits a ramified lift exactly when \\(a=b=0\\). Bézout therefore bounds the ramified base set by \\(\\deg(a)\\deg(b)\\le D(D-d)\\). Deleting a base point removes at most its \\(p+1\\) incidences, so its normalized cost is \\(1/p^2\\).\n\nIf a graph line were identically ramified, both \\(a\\) and \\(b\\) would vanish identically on its base line, contradicting their coprimality.\n\n### [P7] Algebra of the singular construction — proved\n\nThe polynomial \\(H\\) has degree \\(d+1\\), so \\(B=XZ+H(Y)\\) has weighted degree \\(D=d+1<p\\). As a polynomial in \\(Z\\), its coefficients \\(X,H(Y)\\) are coprime; hence it is primitive and absolutely irreducible by Gauss's lemma. It is consequently squarefree, and\n\\[\nB_Z=X,\n\\qquad \\gcd(B,B_Z)=1.\n\\]\nThe usual normalized discriminant of a degree-one polynomial is \\(1\\), whereas\n\\[\n\\operatorname{Res}_Z(B,B_Z)=X.\n\\]\nThus the raw resultant curve is a smooth absolutely irreducible line. At each lift \\((0,c_j,0)\\), however,\n\\[\nB_X=Z=0,\n\\quad B_Y=H'(c_j)=0,\n\\quad B_Z=X=0,\n\\]\nso the auxiliary hypersurface is singular there.\n\n### [P8] The full table and exact incidence counts — proved\n\nFor \\(j\\in\\{1,\\ldots,s\\}\\) and \\(m\\in\\mathbb F_p\\), take\n\\[\nL_{j,m}(t)=(t,c_j+mt),\n\\qquad\nP_{j,m}(t)=-\\frac{H(c_j+mt)}t.\n\\]\nThe quotient is a polynomial: for \\(m\\ne0\\), the double root at \\(c_j\\) makes the numerator divisible by \\(t^2\\); for \\(m=0\\), it is the zero polynomial. Its degree is at most \\(d\\), and\n\\[\nB(L_{j,m}(t),P_{j,m}(t))\\equiv0.\n\\]\nDefine\n\\[\nf(x,y)=\n\\begin{cases}\n-H(y)/x,&x\\ne0,\\\\\n0,&x=0,\n\\end{cases}\n\\]\nand set every unselected line label to zero. Every selected line is fully accepted, including its point \\(t=0\\). The \\(sp\\) lines are distinct, so they contribute agreement \\(s/(p+1)\\). Since \\(B_Z(L_{j,m}(t),P_{j,m}(t))=t\\), each has exactly one ramified accepted parameter. The normalized selected ramified mass is therefore\n\\[\n\\frac{sp}{p^2(p+1)}=\\frac{s}{p(p+1)}.\n\\]\nAt \\(p=103,d=101\\), \\(s=51\\), \\(D=102\\), and \\(sp=5{,}253\\).\n\n### [P9] Absence of a common global root and interpolation minimality — proved\n\nIf a total-degree-at-most-\\(d\\) polynomial \\(Q\\) restricted to every selected label, then\n\\[\nR(X,Y)=XQ(X,Y)+H(Y)\n\\]\nwould have total degree at most \\(D=d+1\\) and vanish identically on \\(sp>D\\) distinct affine lines. Their distinct line equations would all divide \\(R\\), forcing \\(R=0\\). This is impossible because \\(X\\nmid H(Y)\\).\n\nThere is also no nonzero graph interpolant of weighted degree at most \\(d\\). Such an interpolant must be \\(aZ+b(X,Y)\\) with constant \\(a\\). If \\(a=0\\), then \\(b\\) vanishes on more than \\(d\\) lines and is zero. If \\(a\\ne0\\), then \\(-b/a\\) is the forbidden polynomial \\(Q\\). Since \\(B\\) itself has weight \\(d+1\\), it is a minimum-weight interpolant.\n\n### [P10] Monic smooth-discriminant stress test — proved\n\nLet \\(2d\\le D<p\\), put \\(r=D-d\\), choose distinct \\(a_1,\\ldots,a_r\\in\\mathbb F_p\\), and set \\(A(X)=\\prod_i(X-a_i)\\). Then\n\\[\nB_{\\mathrm{sm}}=Z^2+A(X)Z+Y\n\\]\nis monic in \\(Z\\), has weight \\(D\\), and is smooth and absolutely irreducible because \\((B_{\\mathrm{sm}})_Y=1\\). Its discriminant\n\\[\n\\Delta=A(X)^2-4Y\n\\]\nis also smooth and absolutely irreducible. Nevertheless, on \\(L(t)=(t,0)\\) with the legal ambient-degree-\\(d\\) label \\(P_L=0\\),\n\\[\n(B_{\\mathrm{sm}})_Z(L(t),0)=A(t)\n\\]\nhas exactly \\(D-d\\) roots. Thus neither monicity nor smooth absolute irreducibility improves the pointwise per-line root bound. This agrees with [P5], because these roots occur at distinct base points and only one tangent direction is allowed at each.\n\n### [P11] Dense singular stress test — proved\n\nFor \\(p>4d+1\\), let \\(D=2d\\), choose distinct nonzero \\(a_1,\\ldots,a_{d-1}\\), put \\(g(X)=\\prod_i(X-a_i)\\), and define\n\\[\nB_{\\mathrm{den}}=Z^2-XYg(X)^2.\n\\]\nThe odd valuation of \\(Y\\) shows that \\(XYg^2\\) is not a square in \\(\\overline{\\mathbb F}_p(X,Y)\\); hence \\(B_{\\mathrm{den}}\\) is absolutely irreducible. For each nonzero square \\(s=c_s^2\\),\n\\[\nL_s(t)=(t,st),\n\\qquad P_s(t)=c_stg(t)\n\\]\nis a degree-\\(d\\) graph root. There are \\((p-1)/2>D\\) such lines, and \\((B_{\\mathrm{den}})_Z=2Z\\) has exactly the \\(d=D-d\\) roots \\(0,a_1,\\ldots,a_{d-1}\\) on every graph. A polynomial root would satisfy \\(Q^2=XYg^2\\), contradicting the odd \\(Y\\)-valuation. All these ramified lifts are singular, so [P5] is not contradicted.\n\n### [P12] Tempting replacements for simplicity — refuted\n\nThe following claims are false:\n\n- absolute irreducibility plus more than \\(D\\) graph lines forces a global polynomial root without a simple common lift;\n- a smooth absolutely irreducible raw-resultant curve controls graph-direction multiplicity;\n- smooth absolute irreducibility of a monic discriminant gives \\(o(D-d)\\) ramified parameters on every graph line.\n\nThey are refuted respectively by [P7]–[P9], [P7]–[P8], and [P10]. The correct positive statement is [P5]: smoothness must hold at the lifted point on \\(B=0\\), not merely generically or on the projected resultant curve.\n\n### [P13] Exponent consequence — conditional\n\nUnder the KTZ upper envelope \\(D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\), [P3] purges geometrically reducible factors at normalized cost \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\), and [P5] would charge smooth ramification by \\(1/(p+1)\\). These are improvements over a blanket \\(D/p\\) charge, but only after assigning incidences to a fixed factor and proving the required smoothness.\n\nThe explicit constructions show that absolute irreducibility does not supply that smoothness. If singular incidences are still charged by \\(D/p\\), the comparison\n\\[\n\\sqrt{\\frac d{\\epsilon p}}=O(\\epsilon)\n\\]\nagain yields \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\). This is an architecture diagnosis, not a proof that every possible method must remain cubic.\n\n## Exponent Ledger\n\n| Stage | Input scale | Exact loss | Output or requirement | Status |\n|---|---:|---:|---:|---|\n| KTZ benchmark | \\(\\epsilon\\ge C(d/p)^{1/3}\\) | Published proof losses | global agreement \\(c\\epsilon\\) | quoted/proved |\n| KTZ reconstruction | \\(|\\mathcal R|\\le6400p/\\epsilon\\) | \\(D/p\\le1280\\sqrt{d/(\\epsilon p)}+16/p\\) | \\(\\epsilon^3=\\Omega(d/p)\\) suffices | proved reconstruction |\n| Frobenius purification | factor weights \\(\\delta_i\\) | \\(\\sum_i\\delta_i^2/[4dp(p+1)]\\le D^2/[4dp(p+1)]\\) | only absolute factors remain | proved |\n| Purification at KTZ envelope | \\(D^2=O(dp/\\epsilon)\\) | \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\) | needs \\(\\epsilon^2p=\\Omega(1)\\) to be \\(O(\\epsilon)\\) | conditional |\n| Smooth fixed factor | at most \\(p^2\\) edges | \\(1/(p+1)\\) | needs \\(\\epsilon p=\\Omega(1)\\) | proved |\n| Linear regime | \\(d\\le D<2d\\) | \\(D(D-d)/p^2\\) | vertex-based cleanup | proved |\n| Singular table | \\(D=d+1\\), \\(s=\\lfloor(D/2)\\rfloor\\) | \\(s/[p(p+1)]\\) | \\(\\epsilon_{\\rm tab}\\ge s/(p+1)\\); no global-agreement claim | proved |\n| Residual per-line method | \\(D=O(\\sqrt{dp/\\epsilon})\\) | \\(D/p=O(\\sqrt{d/(\\epsilon p)})\\) | cubic threshold remains | conditional |\n\nThe new arguments use one explicit union bound in [P4]. They use no Markov inequality, Cauchy–Schwarz inequality, point-line mixing, interpolation multiplicity, or division by a derivative.\n\n## Counterexample Attempts\n\n1. **Degree-drop discriminant attack:** successful against normalized discriminants. For \\(B=XZ+H(Y)\\), \\(\\operatorname{Disc}_ZB=1\\) but the raw resultant is \\(X\\); the omitted fiber contains every singular accepted lift.\n2. **Absolute plane-curve attack:** unsuccessful as a route to soundness. The raw-resultant curve \\(X=0\\) is already smooth, absolutely irreducible, and has the expected \\(p\\) rational points. The missing statistic is directional multiplicity above its points.\n3. **Monic repair:** unsuccessful. The construction in [P10] removes leading-coefficient degeneration and keeps both the hypersurface and discriminant smooth, but still attains \\(D-d\\) roots on one line.\n4. **Many-direction repair:** unsuccessful. The constructions in [P8] and [P11] have more than \\(D\\) graph lines and no global polynomial root; the common lifted points are singular.\n5. **Endpoint \\(d=p-1\\):** the attempted singular construction fails under \\(D<p\\). Here \\(D=d\\), and every primitive \\(Z\\)-dependent interpolant directly yields \\(Z-Q\\).\n6. **Adversarial full tables:** [P8] is a full table with uniform sampling and explicit agreement. It is not a soundness counterexample: for example, its point table has substantial structured zero sets, so some global polynomial can have nontrivial agreement even though none matches every selected label.\n\n## Characteristic Audit\n\n- Because \\(d>100\\) and \\(d<p\\), the prime \\(p\\) is odd. The uses of \\(2^{-1}\\) and nonsquares are safe.\n- [P1] identifies the actual inseparability threshold \\(\\operatorname{wdeg}B<dp\\). The commonly imposed \\(D<p\\) is stronger and is needed for other polynomial-identity/root-count steps, not for vertical separability itself.\n- Frobenius in [P3] is used only to compare absolute factors of an \\(\\mathbb F_p\\)-polynomial. The test remains over the prime field; there is no extension-field test or descent.\n- The quotient in [P8] is exact polynomial division. No value \\(t=0\\) is inverted.\n- The standard discriminant/resultant distinction is explicit. For degree one, normalizing by the leading coefficient loses degree-dropping fibers.\n- The lower boundary is tested at \\(p=103,d=101,D=102\\). No case with \\(d\\le100\\) is invoked.\n- The construction covers \\(d=p-2\\). At \\(d=p-1\\), the separate linear argument yields a graph polynomial immediately.\n- Local labels have degree at most the ambient \\(d\\); global degree is total degree. No individual-degree substitution is made.\n- The selected lines in [P8] use all \\(p\\) nonvertical directions, with \\(s\\) translates in each direction. The obstruction is therefore not caused by concentration in a small direction set.\n\n## Limitations\n\nThis note does not prove a bivariate soundness theorem beyond KTZ, does not claim a new exponent, and does not bound the best global agreement for its explicit tables. It shows only that an absolute-factor/discriminant strategy must separately control singular accepted lifts.\n\nThe purification loss \\(O(1/(\\epsilon p))\\) requires \\(\\epsilon^2p=\\Omega(1)\\) if discarded outright. That condition is harmless under the cubic benchmark but can fail in parts of the intended \\((d/p)^{1-o(1)}\\) regime. A more refined component argument is still needed.\n\nAlthough [P9] proves that \\(B=XZ+H(Y)\\) is a minimum-weight interpolant for its displayed graph constraints, this note does not prove that the exact randomized reference-set and component-selection stages of KTZ necessarily output that factor. Conversely, it does not prove that those stages eliminate it.\n\nFinally, Weil-type plane-curve estimates count rational points, whereas this bottleneck concerns accepted graph directions and multiplicities above those points. If\n\n`\u03b4\u00b3 \u2265 K d\u03c3/p`,\n\nthen there is a polynomial `Q\u2208F_p[X,Y]` of total degree at most `d` with\n\n`Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)] \u2265 \u03b4/8000`.\n\nThus, if `\u03b4\u2265\u03b5/2`, the conclusion is at least `\u03b5/16000`. With all accepted edges and \u03c3\u22641, the sufficient threshold is `\u03b5\u226510^5(d/p)^(1/3)`. Under the additional structural condition `\u03c3\u2264A\u03b4`, it becomes the conditional square-root threshold `\u03b4\u2265sqrt(10^15 A d/p)`.\n\n**Lemma B \u2014 prime vertical derivative.** If `B\u2208F_p[X,Y,Z]` is squarefree, primitive as a polynomial in `Z`, and has total degree below `p`, then `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`.\n\n**Theorem C \u2014 modal obstruction at the legal lower boundary.** Let `d=101`, `N=(d+1)(d+2)/2=5253`, and\n\n`r=floor(log p/(4 log log p))`.\n\nFor every sufficiently large prime, explicitly every prime `p\u2265max{\u2308e^32\u2309,100N\u00b2}`, there are a point table and constant line labels, hence labels of degree at most 101, such that\n\n`r/(130p) \u2264 \u03b5 \u2264 50r/p`,  while  `Agr_101(f)<2/p`.\n\nConsequently, for every fixed `C,c>0`, arbitrarily large primes admit `\u03b5\u2265C\u00b7101/p` but `Agr_101(f)<c\u03b5`.\n\n**Proposition D \u2014 near-p information baseline.** For every `101\u2264d<p` and every point table,\n\n`Agr_d(f) \u2265 (d+1)(d+2)/(2p\u00b2)`.\n\n## Proof or Conditional Proof\n\n**[P1] (proved) Carrier pruning.** Set `k0=floor(\u03b4p/100)`. Iteratively delete point vertices and line vertices whose current carrier degree is below `k0`. Point deletions remove at most `p\u00b2k0` edges and line deletions at most `p(p+1)k0` edges. In normalized incidence measure the loss is at most\n\n`k0/(p+1)+k0/p < \u03b4/50`.\n\nKeep the weaker bound that the remaining graph `G0` has edge mass at least `\u03b4/4`. It has minimum degree `k0`; its line set `L0` has normalized measure \u03bb satisfying `\u03b4/4\u2264\u03bb\u2264\u03c3`.\n\n**[P2] (proved) Support-sensitive selector.** Select each line of `L0` independently with probability `\u03b8=8/k0`. The hypothesis and `\u03c3\u2265\u03b4` imply\n\n`\u03b4\u00b2\u226510^15 d/p`,  `\u03b4p\u2265sqrt(10^15dp)>3\u00b710^9`,\n\nso `k0\u2265\u03b4p/200`. For a fixed `L\u2208L0`, coverage indicators at distinct neighbors of `L` depend on disjoint sets of other lines. Each has success probability above `3/4`; Hoeffding therefore bounds failure to cover half the neighbors by `exp(\u2212k0/8)`. Since `k0\u22658 log(4p(p+1))`, a union bound over all affine lines costs less than `1/4`.\n\nIf `r=|R|`, then `E[r]=\u03b8|L0|\u2265200(p+1)` and `Var(r)\u2264E[r]`. Chebyshev puts `r` between half and twice its mean with failure below `1/4`. Some deterministic selection consequently satisfies both coverage and\n\n`100(p+1)\u2264r\u226416|L0|/k0\u22646400\u03c3p/\u03b4`.\n\nThese are the only Hoeffding, selector union, and Chebyshev losses.\n\n**[P3] (proved) Weighted interpolation.** Give `X,Y,Z` weights `1,1,d` and set\n\n`D=16(floor(sqrt(dr))+1)`.\n\nThen `D\u00b2>256dr` and KTZ's monomial count gives `dim(V_D)\u2265D\u00b3/(64d)>r(D+1)`. Each formal identity `A(L(t),P_L(t))=0` imposes at most `D+1` coefficient equations, so a nonzero interpolant exists. Moreover,\n\n`D\u22641280 sqrt(d\u03c3p/\u03b4)+16\u22641280\u03b4p/sqrt(10^15)+16<\u03b4p/10000`.\n\nThus `D<p`, `D<k0/2`, and, for `k1=floor(\u03b4p/1000)`, `D<k1/2`. Also `r>D`. A nonzero `Z`-independent polynomial of degree at most `D` cannot vanish identically on more than `D` affine lines, so `A_Z\u22600`. Choosing minimum weighted degree removes repeated factors and makes `A` squarefree.\n\n**[P4] (proved) Identity extension and formal content removal.** Every `L\u2208L0` has more than `k0/2>D` distinct accepted points that also lie on selected accepted lines. At each such point the two line labels equal the same value `f(x)`. Hence the degree-at-most-`D` polynomial `A(L(t),P_L(t))` has more than `D` distinct roots and is identically zero.\n\nWrite `A=H(X,Y)B(X,Y,Z)`, where `H` is the gcd of the coefficients in `Z`. At most `deg(H)\u2264D` base lines satisfy `H|_L=0` identically. On every other retained line, `H(L(t))B(L(t),P_L(t))=0` in the integral domain `F_p[t]`; hence `B(L(t),P_L(t))=0`. This is formal polynomial division, not division by values of `H`. No root multiplicities are counted.\n\n**[P5] (proved) Prime vertical-derivative lemma.** Factor the squarefree primitive polynomial as `B=c\u220fP_i` into distinct irreducibles over `F_p`. Primitivity implies that every `P_i` genuinely depends on `Z`. Since `deg_Z(P_i)<p`, its derivative `(P_i)_Z` is nonzero, and its smaller degree implies `P_i` does not divide `(P_i)_Z`. Modulo `P_i`,\n\n`B_Z = (P_i)_Z \u220f_{j\u2260i}P_j \u22600`.\n\nThus no irreducible factor of `B` divides `B_Z`, proving `gcd(B,B_Z)=1`. No irreducibility over the algebraic closure is required. This replaces, in the prime-field regime only, KTZ's generic directional derivative.\n\n**[P6] (proved) Degenerate-root deletion.** Apply KTZ's resultant line bound to the coprime pair `(B,B_Z)`. Delete the at most `D` content lines, at most `D(D\u22121)` lines on which the two graph identities degenerate together, and at most `D` zeros of `B_Z(L(t),P_L(t))` on every other line. Their total normalized edge mass is bounded by\n\n`D/[p(p+1)] + D(D\u22121)/[p(p+1)] + D/p < \u03b4/16`.\n\nPruning both sides at degree `k1=floor(\u03b4p/1000)` costs at most\n\n`k1/(p+1)+k1/p<\u03b4/500`.\n\nThe surviving graph `G1` has edge mass at least `\u03b4/8`, minimum degree `k1`, and `B_Z(x,f(x))\u22600` at every surviving point. No discriminant or Markov inequality appears.\n\n**[P7] (proved) Hensel lifting and propagation.** At a surviving point translate the base coordinates to `(0,0)` and put `\u03b1=f(0,0)`. In `F_p[[X,Y]]`, construct a root `\u03a6=\u03b1+\u03a6_1+\u03a6_2+\u2026` recursively by homogeneous degree. At stage `j`, the degree-`j` residual is canceled uniquely by division by the scalar `B_Z(0,0,\u03b1)`. Thus no factorial is inverted.\n\nEvery incident line polynomial is the same unique root after restriction to that line. There are more than `D` incident directions. Therefore every homogeneous part `\u03a6_j` with `d<j\u2264D` vanishes on more than `D\u2265j` projective directions and is zero. Let `Q` be the truncation through degree `d`. The polynomial `B(X,Y,Q)` has degree at most `D` and all terms through degree `D` vanish, so it is identically zero. Simple-root uniqueness propagates the same `Q` across every edge of the connected component, and `Q=f` at all of its point vertices.\n\n**[P8] (proved) Component mixing and recovery.** For a component let `a,b,e` denote its normalized point, line, and edge measures. Put `\u03ba=k1/p` and `u=1/sqrt(p+1)`. Minimum degree and point-line mixing give\n\n`e\u2265\u03baa/2`,  `e\u2265\u03bab`,  and  `e\u2264ab+u sqrt(ab)`.\n\nThe theorem hypothesis gives `u<\u03b4/8000\u2264\u03ba/4`. If `a<\u03ba/4`, the last two inequalities imply `9b\u2264a`, which contradicts the first inequality. If `b<\u03ba/4`, they imply `a\u2264b`, which contradicts `e\u2265\u03bab`. Hence `a,b\u2265\u03ba/4\u2265\u03b4/8000`. The polynomial from [P7] therefore has global agreement at least `\u03b4/8000`. This is the sole incidence Cauchy\u2013Schwarz loss.\n\n**[P9] (proved) Exact cubic reconstruction.** The dominant scales are\n\n`r=O(\u03c3p/\u03b4)`,  `D=O(sqrt(d\u03c3p/\u03b4))`,  `D=O(\u03b4p)`.\n\nThe first two give the interpolation degree; the last is independently demanded by identity extension, the `D/p` bad-incidence term, and lifting. Squaring the final comparison yields exactly `\u03b4\u00b3=\u03a9(d\u03c3/p)`. The resultant term `D\u00b2/p\u00b2` alone needs only `\u03b4\u00b2=\u03a9(d\u03c3/p)`, and mixing needs only `\u03b4=\u03a9(p^\u22121/2)`; both are weaker here. For \u03c3=1 this is the KTZ cubic exponent.\n\n**[P10] (conditional) Concentrated-carrier exponent.** If additionally `\u03c3\u2264A\u03b4`, [P9] becomes `\u03b4\u00b2=\u03a9(Ad/p)`, giving exponent `1/2`. Since every carrier has `\u03c3\u2265\u03b4`, this support-sensitive interpolation balance cannot exceed exponent `1/2`. This is not an unconditional improvement of the benchmark.\n\n**[P11] (proved) Modal occupancy lower bound.** For Theorem C choose all `p\u00b2` point values independently and uniformly. On a fixed line let `N_a` be the occupancy of value `a`, `M=max_a N_a`, and `Y=\u03a3_a 1[N_a=r]`. For one value,\n\n`Pr[N_a=r] = binom(p,r)p^(\u2212r)(1\u22121/p)^(p\u2212r) \u2265 1/(8r!)`.\n\nHere `r\u00b2\u2264p`, `(1\u22121/p)^p\u22651/4`, and `r!\u2264r^r\u2264p^(1/4)`. Thus `\u03bc=E[Y]\u2265p^(3/4)/8\u22651`. For distinct values, the joint probability of both occupancies equaling `r` is at most `1/(r!)\u00b2`, at most 64 times the product of the lower bounds. Hence `E[Y\u00b2]\u2264\u03bc+64\u03bc\u00b2\u226465\u03bc\u00b2`. Cauchy\u2013Schwarz, equivalently the zero-threshold Paley\u2013Zygmund argument, gives `Pr[Y>0]\u22651/65`, so `E[M]\u2265r/65`.\n\nGive each line a modal constant label. By linearity of expectation across lines\u2014no line independence is asserted\u2014the local agreement `A` satisfies `E[A]\u2265r/(65p)`.\n\n**[P12] (proved) Modal upper concentration.** A factorial-moment union bound gives\n\n`Pr[M\u2265s]\u2264p/s!\u2264p(e/s)^s`.\n\nFor `s0=ceil(4 log p/log log p)`, the tail sums to less than one and `E[M]\u2264s0+1\u226425r`; hence `E[A]\u226425r/p`. Changing one point value changes the modal count on only its `p+1` incident lines and changes `A` by at most `1/p\u00b2`. McDiarmid therefore gives\n\n`Pr[A>50r/p]\u2264exp(\u22121250r\u00b2)\u2264r/(520p)`.\n\nNo Markov inequality is used.\n\n**[P13] (proved) Global union bound and deterministic instance.** There are `p^N` formal total-degree-at-most-101 polynomials, with `N=5253`. For fixed `Q`, its agreement count with random `f` is `Bin(p\u00b2,1/p)`, of mean `p`. Chernoff gives\n\n`Pr[agreements(Q,f)\u22652p]\u2264(e/4)^p`.\n\nUnion over all `p^N` polynomials gives `p^N(e/4)^p\u2264exp(\u2212p/4)\u2264r/(520p)` under the stated lower bound on `p`. Let `G` be the event that all global agreements are below `2/p`, and `H={A\u226450r/p}`. Since `0\u2264A\u22641`,\n\n`E[A\u00b71_{G\u2229H}] \u2265 r/(65p)\u2212r/(520p)\u2212r/(520p) > r/(130p)`.\n\nSome deterministic table in `G\u2229H` therefore has all three bounds in Theorem C.\n\n**[P14] (refuted) Uniform exact-linear soundness.** Suppose constants `C,c>0` made `\u03b5\u2265Cd/p` imply `Agr_d(f)\u2265c\u03b5` uniformly. Fix the legal ambient cap `d=101` and choose a sufficiently large prime with `r\u2265max{130\u00b7101C,260/c}`. Theorem C then has `\u03b5\u2265C\u00b7101/p` but `Agr_101(f)<2/p<c\u03b5`, a contradiction. Thus the exact-linear statement is false. On the other hand, for each fixed `\u03b7>0`,\n\n`\u03b5/(101/p)^(1\u2212\u03b7) \u2264 50r/[101^(1\u2212\u03b7)p^\u03b7] \u2192 0`,\n\nso this construction does not refute a fixed-\u03b7 target.\n\n**[P15] (proved) Near-p information set.** Choose distinct `a_0,\u2026,a_d` and `b_0,\u2026,b_d` and the triangular set `S={(a_i,b_j):i+j\u2264d}`. The Newton products `\u220f_{h<i}(X\u2212a_h)\u220f_{k<j}(Y\u2212b_k)` with `i+j\u2264d` form a triangular evaluation basis on `S`. Hence arbitrary prescribed values on all `|S|=(d+1)(d+2)/2` points extend to a total-degree-at-most-`d` polynomial. Applying this to `f|_S` proves Proposition D. In particular, the lower bound is `(p+1)/(2p)` at `d=p\u22121` and `5253/10609` at `d=101,p=103`.\n\n**[P16] (proved) Diffuse support need not concentrate.** Fix the legal ambient `d\u2265101`, take `f=0`, and on every line choose a degree-`d` label with `d` distinct prescribed parameter roots. Thus local density does not imply `\u03c3=O(\u03b5)`, although this example is harmless for soundness.\n\n**[P17] (refuted as an obstruction) Concentrated good directions.** Let `f` be a product of `d+1` distinct homogeneous linear forms. In each of the corresponding `d+1` projective directions, every affine-line restriction loses its degree-`d+1` leading term and is a legal degree-`d` label. This gives local mass about `(d+1)/(p+1)`. But `Q=0` agrees on the union of the same `d+1` lines through the origin, a \u0398(d/p) fraction. The attempted counterexample already contains the required global polynomial.\n\n**[P18] (refuted safety of omitting simplicity) Branch collision.** For odd `p` and legal ambient cap `d\u2265101`, `B=Z\u00b2\u2212X\u00b2` is squarefree but its two legal branches `Q=X` and `Q=\u2212X` meet at the origin, where `B_Z=0`. Agreement at that incidence cannot select a branch. Vertical-simple-root deletion is therefore logically necessary.\n\n**[P19] (refuted as an active obstruction) Inseparability.** A polynomial with vanishing `Z`-derivative must use positive `Z`-exponents divisible by `p`.
